Data were aggregated across 28 Pcdh enhancer–promoter pairs included in the analysis and 16,399 ORCA traces from mOSNs. Gray bars indicate the number of promoter-to-enhancer measurements per bin. Bin size: 50 nm. Error bars: 95% Wilson binomial confidence intervals around the observed fraction in each bin.

(a) Left: schematic of distance measurements between locus positions and heterochromatin/euchromatin domain centres. For each locus position, dHC − dEC was calculated, where dHC and dEC are distances to the heterochromatin and cluster-specific euchromatin centres, respectively. Negative values indicate greater proximity to the heterochromatin centre; positive values indicate greater proximity to the euchromatin centre. Right: median per-trace dHC − dEC across locus positions in the Pcdhb and Pcdhg clusters for Pcdhb16-transcribing traces with enhancer–promoter contact, Pcdhb16-transcribing traces without enhancer–promoter contact, and non-transcribing Pcdhb16 traces. Vertical dashed lines: Pcdhb16 and its enhancer HS18-22. Red and gray bars: heterochromatic and euchromatic regions, respectively. n: traces per condition. (b) Change in dHC and dEC for Pcdhb16 and HS18-22 in Pcdhb16-transcribing traces with enhancer–promoter contact relative to transcribing traces without enhancer–promoter contact. (c) Median promoter dHC − dEC in transcribing traces without and with enhancer–promoter contact. Each paired set of points represents one Pcdh isoform. For each isoform, dHC − dEC was calculated per trace, then summarized as the median across traces in each contact state. (d) Median enhancer dHC − dEC in transcribing traces without and with enhancer–promoter contact, calculated as in (c). For (c,d), paired points correspond to the same Pcdh isoform or cognate enhancer. Significance was assessed using a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 1.9 × 10−6 and P = 2.6 × 10−5 for (c,d), respectively. 30 Pcdh isoforms were included in the analysis. Arrowheads indicate c-type Pcdh genes or their enhancers. (e) Percent of transcribing traces with and without enhancer–promoter contact for each Pcdh isoform. For all panels, 16,399 ORCA traces from mOSNs were examined; only traces where the relevant promoters and enhancers were detected were included.

(a) Genetic strategy used to generate mouse lines. Black triangles: loxP sites. (b) Immunostaining for RAD21 (top) and SETDB1 (bottom) in heterozygous and homozygous animals. Representative images are shown from one of two independent experiments with similar results. Scale bar: 50 μm. (c) H3K9me3 nChIP-seq over the Pcdh locus in four WT (Omp-GFP) and three Setdb1cKO biological replicates. Data were generated across two independent experiments. The two additional WT replicates in Fig. 5c are shown in Fig. 1h. (d) Top: median distance of each locus position to the heterochromatin (HC) domain centre in Rad21cKO and WT mOSNs. Bottom: Rad21cKO - WT difference. Yellow bars: Pcdh enhancers. (e) Top: mean pairwise entropy for each locus position in Setdb1cKO and WT mOSNs. Entropy was calculated from pairwise distance distributions to all other locus positions and averaged across partners. Bottom: Setdb1cKO - WT difference. Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion brings enhancers into the domain to engage promoters, with transcription initiating from within the domain. After promoter activation, transcription can proceed in the absence of enhancer—promoter engagement. #1276. Galliani warns Malagò: ‘Juventus, Inter and Milan have changed their stance on FIGC president’

Adriano Galliani has hit back at Giovanni Malagò, claiming Juventus, Inter and Milan are among the Serie A clubs who have switched sides in the race for the FIGC presidency.

With quotes via La Gazzetta dello Sport, the two candidates traded light-hearted jabs on Thursday, with the election now just over two weeks away.

Speaking on the sidelines of a CONI council meeting, Malagò suggested he wouldn’t have run in Galliani’s position. He pointed to the U-turn made by the “technical components”, meaning the players’ union (AIC) and the coaches’ association (AIAC).

“What would I have done in Galliani’s place? Honestly, I wouldn’t have stood, given the U-turn by the technical components,” Malagò said. “But Adriano is a friend, and I’ll never say anything that isn’t affectionate. So I say it with a smile, even if I think this view is widely shared.”

Asked whether Galliani was mounting a late comeback, Malagò added: “I’ve never been chasing in this game. It’s an electoral contest like many I’ve fought, even if there have been some strange positions.”

Galliani, the former Milan and Monza executive, had his reply ready when he was approached leaving the PalaEur. He had been there for Italy’s basketball game against Turkey, which Malagò also attended.

“To my friend Giovanni, I’d say I stood because, as well as the technical components, a U-turn was also made by eight or nine Serie A clubs, including big ones like Juventus, Inter and Milan,” he said with a smile.

#1275. 'You can't escape from it': Rasmus Hojlund opens up on the suffocating pressure of playing for Man United - and reveals Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot are 'looking forward to change' under Mauricio Pochettino

Published: 05:31 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 06:12 EST, 25 November 2026

Rasmus Hojlund has laid bare the suffocating pressure of playing for Manchester United and given his insight into what Mauricio Pochettino’s squad will be suffering while marooned in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Dane was back in town this week after spending two seasons at United, mocking Manchester City fans when scoring the opener of Napoli’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.

Hojlund secured a £38million permanent move away from Old Trafford in the summer but remains in touch with plenty of old team-mates and believes the lack of equilibrium at the club has contributed to a steady decline.

‘There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it,’ Hojlund said.

‘It is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad. It is all about trying to be in that middle. I had both the highs and the lows there.

‘The pressure is part of the club, it comes with playing for United. There has been a lot of change but hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.’

Rasmus Hojlund mocked Man City fans after scoring for Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday night

A United supporter, Hojlund laughed off the idea that the club is in a relegation scrap despite their worst start to a season since 1972. And the 23-year-old revealed that the players were ready for ‘change’ following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

‘I spoke with Bruno [Fernandes] and Diogo [Dalot] during the international break and they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,’ Hojlund added.

‘I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best. I am sure they will turn it around this season. They have got a lot of quality. They have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals.

‘It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top. The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth was in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.’

#1274. Better Than Araujo: Man Utd Already Know Priority First Signing For Pochettino

Manchester United are in dire need of a new left-back in January. Lisandro Martinez was used in that position for the 2-2 draw at Sporting CP on Wednesday, after Diogo Dalot was dropped following another dismal performance in the 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool.

Luke Shaw is nearing a return to full fitness, however, and is expected to take back that spot soon, after missing the last seven weeks with a muscle problem. Despite that, Shaw has struggled even when available and United should look to upgrade in the transfer window.

According to Sport Witness, United are showing interest in Sporting left-back Maxi Araujo. It's understood the Reds have been monitoring the Uruguay international for a number of months now, and, of course, saw him up close at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday.

Araujo has a £67million release clause in his contract, but United could get him for less in January. As well as that, he is believed to be 'very open' about making the move to Old Trafford and has previously expressed his desire to play in the Premier League.

It could be a smart signing, but United should avoid Araujo and instead target someone else. While the 26-year-old did win Sporting's second spot-kick as he was fouled by Senne Lammens and was an attacking threat, he has some big flaws to his game.

Indeed, in the draw against United, Araujo lost possession NINE times, completing just 86 per cent of his passes (38/46) and having one out of four successful dribbles. He didn't make a single accurate pass into the box and completed just one successful cross.

Alongside that, Araujo's defending flattered to deceive. He won just 42 per cent (8/19) of his duels, one tackle and committed three fouls. The ex-Puebla and Toluca man started as a left wing-back and often got caught out with Amad Diallo having joy on that side.

While he can be strong going forward, Araujo does struggle defensively and has proven that on a number of occasions this season. None more so than in the 3-2 defeat to LASK in the Champions League last month, where he could have done better for all three goals. He didn't stop the cross for LASK's first, while both the second and third came down his side.

Considering that and the fact United have conceded the most goals (36) in Europe's top five leagues across all competitions this season, the Reds need a more defensive-minded left-back and Newcastle United's Lewis Hall would be perfect.

The Athletic have reported that United remain interested in Hall, and although it could be difficult for them to persuade Newcastle to sell in January, the Reds need to do all they can to sign him. The England international is one of the best left-sided defenders in the Premier League right now and would be an exceptional addition, even if he is expensive.

Defensively, there are not too many better than Hall about. He produced an impressive performance to keep Lamine Yamal quiet in England's famous 3-2 win against Spain earlier this month, and has been a nemesis for many a right-winger in recent times.

He can attack as well. Indeed, in 113 appearances for Newcastle, Hall has directly contributed to 13 goals. Earlier this season, Hall found the net in a 2-1 win at Hull City and grabbed an assist in a 2-2 draw at home against Bournemouth.

United should go all out to bring Hall to Old Trafford. He should be their first-choice target with Araujo and Antonee Robinson behind. Despite their league position, the Reds should be targeting the best in class - and Hall is just that.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe heaped praise on the "outstanding" Hall last season, despite leaving him out of the starting line-up to face Arsenal. “Lewis is an outstanding player and you never for any second doubt his qualities and what he can bring to the team," Howe said, when asked the reason behind Dan Burn's inclusion in the team at left-back.

Meanwhile, Pochettino worked with Hall for a brief period at Chelsea and wished him well as he moved to Newcastle. Acknowledging his potential, the Argentine said: “He was unlucky that he could not play [more], but he has a good future and I hope he can settle well there.”

Thomas Tuchel hailed Hall's progress during the recent international break, saying he made a "big impression" on the England team.

The Red Devils must stay locked on their primary left-back target

#1272. Trinity Rodman pulls out of USA roster for upcoming tournament just hours after shock split from Ben Shelton

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER and DAN MATTHEWS

Published: 22:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 07:55 EST, 25 November 2026

United States women's soccer star Trinity Rodman has backed out of an upcoming tournament hours after reports revealed she is no longer in a relationship with tennis star Ben Shelton.

Rodman was set to take part in the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship window in Texas, but has now pulled out due to what US Soccer called 'a minor shoulder injury' in a statement announcing the roster move.

The statement says the injury occurred during the 2026 NWSL Championship Game last Saturday, where Rodman and the Washington Spirit fell 2-1 to the Kansas City Current. US Soccer has replaced Rodman with Gotham FC winger Jaedyn Shaw.

Rodman's removal comes hours after the Daily Mail was first to report on her split from the American tennis star.

The American sporting couple began dating around March 2025, frequently supporting one another at their various events, but have recently decided to call time on their relationship.

Their conflicting work schedules and constant travel made it too challenging for the couple to continue maintaining their relationship, the Daily Mail understands. However, the pair are believed to remain close, despite their split.

American soccer stat Trinity Rodman has backed out of the USWNT roster for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship taking place beginning later this week

The announcement comes hours after the Daily Mail was first to report her split from longtime boyfriend and tennis star Ben Shelton

US Soccer says Rodman suffered 'a minor shoulder injury' in the 2026 NWSL Championship

The couple were frequently forced to maintain their romance over long distance with Shelton constantly traveling around the globe while playing on the ATP Tour.

Despite multiple sacrifices and last-minute trips to attend each other's matches, it appears they could no longer make it work.

The Daily Mail has reached out to both Shelton and Rodman's representatives for comment.

Shelton, 24, suffered defeat in the semi-final of the ATP Finals on Saturday, losing 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7-1) to Carlos Alcaraz in Turin, Italy.

The same evening, Rodman, 24, and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL final to the KC Current.

The following evening, the American tennis star was spotted at Madison Square Garden for the New York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers without Rodman, instead sitting on Celebrity Row alongside a friend and actress Inde Navarette.

The couple first went public with their relationship in March 2025 following speculation from fans.

Mystery surrounded the early stages of their relationship, as they initially dropped a playful hint as part of a TikTok trend last March then 'hard launched' their romance soon afterwards.

Their conflicting work schedules made it too challenging to maintain their relationship

The sporting power couple went public with their relationship around March 2025

Rodman was a near-permanent fixture in Shelton's box throughout the US Open in September.

The USWNT star and the Spirit had played an NWSL game in Washington on the day of the final but Rodman left the capital almost immediately after the final whistle to make the mad dash to New York for Shelton's final.

The forward was captured crying inside Arthur Ashe Stadium in the wake of her boyfriend's loss to Alexander Zverev.

Rodman, the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, had cheered on the World No 4 at multiple other events, making her Wimbledon debut in May 2025.

Meanwhile, the tennis superstar was every bit the supportive boyfriend when he consoled Rodman after her team lost the NWSL championship game last November.

The World No 4 attended the Knicks game on Sunday, one day after losing the ATP semifinal

Rodman and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL Championship to the KC Current on Saturday

The Washington Spirit were stunned by underdogs Gotham FC in California, as footage from the game showed Shelton consoling an emotional Rodman as she burst into tears on the sidelines.

Shelton opened up on the challenges of their relationship in September, admitting that it was tough for the couple to continuously make time for one another.

'It is really difficult,' the Grand Slam finalist told US Weekly. 'I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.'

He added: 'Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I'd say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We're not where we want to be yet, we're not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time.

'This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.'

#1271. Ben Jacobs Names 3 Right-Backs Arsenal Are Targeting In January Transfer Window

Arsenal do not traditionally use the January transfer window to do lots of business, but this season may be different.

The Gunners sit pretty at the top of the Premier League table, six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City who sit second and third currently.

But they may look to strengthen their squad when the winter window opens and manager Mikel Arteta is targeting a right-back and a central midfielder.

GIVEMESPORT senior football correspondent Ben Jacobs believes the Gunners will look in the market in January, but may wait until the summer of 2027 to add significantly to their ranks.

Arsenal have suffered with a number of injuries already this season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber missing the start of the campaign, while Bukayo Saka, Martin Zubimendi and more recently David Raya are now sidelined.

Timber has had to cover at centre-back on occasions this season, with Ben White playing at right-back and it is therefore no surprise that they are potentially looking at reinforcements in the full-back area.

And Jacobs has named three potential targets in his exclusive GMS newsletter.

He said: "My information is that Arsenal will be looking for another midfielder, but before we talk about that particular area, we have to think about other pressing positions that Arsenal may focus on.

"As far as the winter is concerned, right-back is relatively high in Arsenal’s thinking, so maybe in the winter, they explore that, if not, it’ll be summer 2027. So yes, midfielder is important, and that is even after the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, but right-back is another area.

"Arsenal are one of the clubs that have looked historically at Malo Gusto, along with Manchester City and even Manchester United in weeks gone by, but the challenge for all three of these clubs is price. £75million was what Chelsea wanted over the summer. If that drops, and Gusto becomes a market opportunity, then there’s several clubs, including from within England, that might decide to advance on Gusto. City were maybe the most concrete on Gusto over the summer, but nothing developed, as I say, because Chelsea’s asking price was just a little bit too high.

"You’ve got David Boly and also Ivan Fresneda, two players that are on Arsenal’s radar too, so they’ll be in the market for some form of right-back, for sure.”

#1270. Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an important moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb

“The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix

Iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

Ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

There will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully launches it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

As expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

Gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

Once again, Liverpool break through Gakpo. This time, it comes from a Brighton corner, but Gakpo’s cross for Isak at the back post is read by Dunk.

In his first involvement since entering the action, Nyoni ends a slick Brighton move by taking the ball off De Cuyper’s toe in the penalty area with a much-needed clearance. He seems to be limping after he was caught by De Cuyper.

Wirtz’s game is over and he departs to be replaced by Nyoni in Liverpool’s first change.

After some treatment for Wirtz, Vuskovic eventually takes the free kick. It’s in such an inviting position, but the defender gets too power on his strike and whips it over the bar.

This game is still very much in the balance, even though Liverpool have a two goal advantage, and it speaks volumes about both teams’ commitment to attack. The questions the respective head coaches are asking of their players are relentless but the players are responding by being adventurous in how they attack and where they want to get on the ball. How Andoni Iraola and Fabian Hurzeler deploy their substitutes will be significant.

Liverpool are holding firm, with Brighton yet to create an opportunity in this second half. Ayari is apprehended by Wirtz to win a free kick on the edge of the area. Despite committing the foul, Wirtz has stayed down and is clutching his ankle.

Brighton make another change and it’s a straight swap in midfield as Yalcouye replaces Chema Andres, who hobbles off the pitch.

With Brighton requiring at least two goals to avoid defeat, they’ll need to push a lot of men forward, which will open up space for Liverpool to exploit on the break. If there is one, the next goal in this game is crucial.

Liverpool break through Gakpo, who sprints from inside his own half into the penalty. He tries to release Isak, but his pass is intercepted by Vuskovic as he’s swarmed by the Brighton defence. Gakpo waited too long and should have played the pass earlier.

Kerkez isn’t switched on and fails to deal with a long ball, allowing Gomez to race in behind. Van Dijk covers Kerkez and blocks Gomez’s pass, with Kostoulas sprinting up in support.

We are back under way for the second half. Hurzeler has made one half-time alteration, with Hinshelwood replacing Boscagli, who was booked just before the break. Meanwhile, Liverpool are unchanged as they look to protect their two-goal advantage.

Wirtz’s wickedly deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s neat finish from close range mean Liverpool are two goals in front against Brighton. The visitors have also looked dangerous going forward, with Ayari wasting a golden chance when the score was still goalless, before hitting the post in the 36th minute. As it stands, this result would move Liverpool into fourth and a point behind Brighton, who need a massive second-half performance.

Two goals to the good for @LFC 😮‍💨 A Pascal Gross own goal puts the Reds ahead, before Alexander Isak fires in the second 🔴 https://t.co/AglQOyUIoY

Brighton are desperate to find a goal before the break as Kostoulas’ fierce shot is batted away by Alisson, whose goal is living a charmed life. Boscagli then receives a yellow card for blocking Barcola’s off-the-ball run.

No getting away from the fact that Brighton simply haven’t got started and it’s a huge surprise. What chances they have had came from Liverpool’s own shortcomings and it is impossible to think they will be so off the pace in the second period. Fabian Hurzeler has remained composed, which is more than can be said for Oliver Boscagli, who looks like he is playing pass the parcel, so anxious is he to get rid of the ball - often with a mistake.

On the counter, Gomez tries to find Ayari with a pass, but Jacquet’s touch knocks the ball out of Liverpool’s box. There will be three minutes of added time to end this half.

Araujo forces a save as he sprints forward from his right-back position to receive a clipped pass from Mac Allister, before shooting from a tight angle to sting the palms of Verbruggen with a drilled effort.

Gakpo drives at Brighton’s defence and then nearly squeezes a low cross to the supporting Isak, but Dunk’s crucial intervention with his outstretched leg prevents a chance.

Off the post for Brighton. Ayari shoots from an incredibly long way out as Brighton dispossess Mac Allister and Jacquet, however his curling effort agonisingly bounces against the post and out, with Alisson well beaten.

Despite falling two goals behind in this first half, Brighton have recorded 83% possession over the previous five minutes.

There’s a small confrontation between Vuskovic and Gakpo, which is quickly checked and cleared by VAR. In the next passage of play, Kerkez tees up Gakpo, who bursts into the box and reaches the byline, but his cross is blocked by Dunk.

A smooth Brighton move ends with Jacquet making a crucial block to deny Kostoulas from close range. Liverpool eventually scramble it clear. That’s a reminder of the threat that Brighton can pose.

Brighton look stunned. Since Ayari missed that chance, they’ve been swarmed by Liverpool, whose forwards are in the mood for some goals today.

Two goals in quick succession propel Liverpool into a commanding lead. So much credit must go to Barcola. He closes down Boscagli, beats the defender to the loose ball with his blistering pace and then delivers a pinpoint cross towards Isak, who gets across his marker at the near post to direct a first-time finish into the far bottom corner.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb

Gakpo bursts in behind Brighton’s defence and outpaces Vuskovic. From a tight angle, the winger shoots, forcing Verbruggen into a decent save. Liverpool are looking very slick in forward areas.

Brighton pay for that missed opportunity at the other end. Araujo’s cross isn’t properly cleared and the ball falls to Wirtz, whose driven effort takes a deflection off Gross and spins into the bottom corner. It’s been awarded as an own-goal. Just a couple of minutes earlier, Ayari should have put Brighton ahead. Instead, they find themselves a goal behind.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR

Florian Wirtz is taking the acclaim but that looks very much like it will be a Pascal Gross own goal. Whether it is credited to him or not, his strength to win possession and keep Liverpool on the front foot was hugely important. You wouldn’t say he is beaming from ear to ear but let’s see how he is at the final whistle. The first goal in this contest had the potential to be hugely important.

Brighton miss a golden chance. Gomez threads a delightful ball past Van Dijk through to Gross, who unselfishly squares it to Ayari. However, the Sweden international sweeps a first-time effort over the bar with the goal gaping. Brighton should be ahead.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP

Barcola tries to race onto a loose ball, but Verbruggen rushes out of his box to beat the pacey winger to it.

Liverpool’s fast start continues as Wirtz curls an exquisite pass from a wide position around Brighton’s defence for Isak to latch onto. The striker can’t take the ball in his stride, allowing Vuskovic to clear. Gakpo then bends a whipped effort into Verbruggen’s arms.

Brighton are currently playing with 10 men due to Kadioglu’s absence as Liverpool apply some pressure. The visitors eventually clear Wirtz’s searching cross. Confirmation of that change sees Costinha replace Kadioglu in Brighton’s backline.

There’s an early issue for Brighton’s Kadioglu, who is sit on the deck clutching his hip. He bumped into Wirtz and Gravenberch in quick succession as he attempted to win the ball. Hurzeler could be forced into a change here.

We are under way at Anfield. Can Iraola get his first home league win as Liverpool boss or will high-flying Brighton continue to upset the odds and close the gap on Manchester City and Arsenal at the top?

Captains Van Dijk and Dunk lead their respective sides out onto the Anfield pitch in windy conditions. Brighton are four points ahead and two places above Liverpool in the league table. Does that make Liverpool the underdogs in their own back yard?

Welcome to Anfield, where we have just had four seasons in 10 minutes: rain was overtaken by sunshine, all the while the wind has been blowing past itself, the kind that wouldn’t just turn an umbrella inside out but carry you off into the distance. Racing was abandoned at Aintree, which is just two miles away, early this morning but there have been no such worries at Anfield. The pitch is actually well sheltered from the elements, so hopefully it won’t impact on the game too much. These sides both want to play football and we can safely say (famous last words) that it won’t be 0-0 at 90 minutes.

Even by his prodigious standards, this has been a different week for Rio Ngumoha. After the coming-of-age performance against Villarreal, so followed the slew of attention on social media.

A clip of his best moments during the chaotic 4-3 dispatching of the Spaniards, posted on Uefa’s official X account, attracted 1.2 million views and was liked more than 24,000 times. Hot on the heels came another video, this time when he was 11, when he nutmegged a dumbfounded cameraman.

Ngumoha has always had feet that move as quickly as the hands of street artists who perform tricks with cups and balls: now you see it, now you don’t. We live in an age where talent is quickly amplified and this young England international has it in bundles.

You saw it in those exhilarating 74 minutes: Ngumoha had his most touches in a game this campaign (51), most touches in the opposition box (12) and attempted the most dribbles (10), as well as creating the most chances (three) and providing two assists.

It is the first time an 18-year-old has produced such figures in the Champions League since Opta’s European records began in 2008-09.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Liverpool and Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield.

Liverpool are on a three-game winning run in all competitions, and came from two goals behind in their previous outing in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning an enthralling 4-3 victory over Villarreal. Last weekend, Andoni Iraola’s men also initially fell behind against Brentford in the Premier League, but netted two second-half goals through Daniel Munoz and Alexander Isak to win 2-1 as their opponents finished with nine men.

In his programme notes, Liverpool boss Iraola was excited about the prospect of a second game in a week at home. “As someone who believes every single opportunity we have to play a game at this stadium and in front of our supporters is a privilege, I also feel very passionately that this is a period that we should continue to embrace,” he said.

“It is also a spell in which we will carry on being tested because the quality of the opposition dictates that there is no chance of anything else. Villarreal pushed us all the way in midweek and everything about the way Brighton have played so far this season tells us that it would be foolish to expect anything but the same today.”

Brighton have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the Premier League season thanks to their blistering start. Fabian Hurzeler’s side sit third in the table, having scored a whopping 23 goals in their opening seven games, while conceding just five. On Thursday, Brighton were unexpectedly held to a 0-0 draw by Czech outfit Jablonec, ending a run of six straight victories in all competitions. Nevertheless, they’re unbeaten since their 4-3 league loss to Chelsea back on August 30.

Defender Ferdi Kadioglu believes his team’s energy and fitness has played a huge role in their eye-catching form. “If you want to play how we play, you have to be very fit,” he said. “We were already fit last season, but I think it’s more that now everyone really understands what we need to do to win matches. That’s really clear this season, and everyone is doing it. Everyone is really focused on their task and doing it very well so far.”

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news following shortly.

#1269. Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3,4,5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6,7,8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

Wiring diagram for the DC and RF lines used to measure the device, with properties and components detailed in the legend. Additional details can be found in ‘Measurement set-up’ in Methods.

a, Detailed schematic of the pulse sequence, showing the various stages of the protocol. b, p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration and pulse ramp time. Parity oscillations remain visible even for slow ramp duration up to approximately 75 ns. An oscillation as a function of ramp duration is also visible at zero pulse duration, indicating that the qubit evolves partially during the ramp of the coupling pulse. c, Time trace and corresponding histogram of the readout signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) with the left chain on resonance and the right-chain QDs off-resonance, using 400 μs readout time. Transitions between \(| e\rangle \) and \(| o\rangle \) are attributed to quasiparticle poisoning. d, Dwell time histogram from c. e, p(e∣e), p(o∣e), p(e∣o), and p(o∣o) while varying the pulse amplitude VC and ramp time. For fast ramps (≲5 ns), parity mixing is observed between the chain and the dot. We attribute this to a diabatic excitation of the coupled system, which rapidly decoheres before the final measurement. In the main text, we use ramp times of 25 ns to avoid these excitations. For pulse amplitudes ≲11.5 mV, no parity mixing is observed, which we use to roughly identify when QDC passes through resonance. f, Schematic of the configuration for the measurements in c-e. g-j, Same as c-f, but for the right chain, with the QDs of the left chain off-resonance. In panel i, parity mixing between the chain and QDC is observed for ramp times  ≲ 10 ns, indicating a slightly weaker coupling between QDC and the right chain versus the left chain.

Readout characterization using time traces of the reflected resonator signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\), measured for three different amounts of detuning with the coupler QD kept fixed far from resonance. Thresholds used for single-shot state identification are obtained by fitting a Gaussian mixture model. The detuning configuration in (e-g) is used for qubit readout. a, Schematic representation of the readout configuration with both chains on resonance. b, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in a. Residual coupling between the chains results in inter-chain hopping that is faster than the readout time of 500 μs, preventing readout in a single shot. The two quantum capacitance signals corresponding to the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) states are partially averaged which makes them difficult to distinguish from the \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) states. c, As in a, but with both chains detuned from resonance. d, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in c. The slight detuning suppresses inter-chain hopping, though it remains too fast for high-fidelity single-shot readout. Two distinctive regions can be observed: When the system is in the global even state, rapid jumps between \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| ee\rangle \) are visible. When the system is poisoned, it enters the global odd manifold. Transitions between \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) are not resolved because they produce similar readout signals. e, As in c but with both chains detuned further from resonance. f, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in e. The two computational states \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) correspond to the red and blue signals, and can now clearly be resolved. The green signal contains both leakage states of the odd global parity manifold (\(| eo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \)). Due to the antisymmetric detuning where the ground state of one dot is full and the other is empty, the \(| oo\rangle \) state is energetically favored over the \(| ee\rangle \) state, resulting in a skewed population between the two. Transitions are mainly observed between the even and odd global manifolds. The signal-to-noise ratios between the leakage distribution and the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) distributions are 2.88 ± 0.28 and 2.76 ± 0.09, respectively. Integrating the fitted Gaussian distributions across the assignment thresholds gives false-leakage probabilities of 0.45% for \(| ee\rangle \) and 0.25% for \(| oo\rangle \), showing that finite readout SNR accounts for only a small fraction of the observed leakage. g, Dwell time histogram of the three observed states, indicating the difference in lifetimes. The shortest measured state lifetime in this readout configuration is 8.3 ms, corresponding to a probability of approximately 5.8% for a state transition during the 500 μs integration window. The trace is acquired with the coupler QD kept far from resonance, showing that state switching on this timescale is already present in the readout configuration. These transitions include both residual inter-chain hopping and quasiparticle-poisoning events and can produce time-averaged signals that are assigned as leakage for pulsed measurements.

Conditional probabilities at the simultaneous sweet spot for the two chains in both the even and odd global parity manifolds, corresponding to Extended Data Fig. 5g but extended to larger pulse amplitudes. Additional outer lines appear when the energy of the detuned chain is aligned with the first excited state of the other chain. The quadrant in which they appear depends on the initial state of the system, as well as the global parity manifold (‘Interpretation of pulsed charge-stability diagrams’ in Methods). a, Left chain in the even manifold. b, Right chain in the even manifold. c, Left chain in the odd manifold. d, Right chain in the odd manifold. The QDR2 resonance is shifted by approximately 3 mV with respect to panel b due to the Coulomb interaction with the additional electron on the parity-switching QD. The odd-manifold measurements include two parity-switch passages, before and after the control sequence. Comparing the background return probabilities in the even- and odd-manifold measurements for initial states \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \) gives single-passage parity-switch fidelity of 99.77 ± 0.03% (‘Parity-switch fidelity’ in Methods).

a, Map of p(oo∣oo) (left) and p(oe∣oe) (right) as a function of the left and right hybrid-gate voltages (VLH and VRH). The diagonal and antidiagonal features of enhanced parity mixing correspond to degeneracies between the qubit basis states. The points labeled c-k indicate the VLH,VRH values used in the remaining panels. b, Schematic representation of the four configurations measured at each point: left- and right-chain pulsed charge-stability diagrams in the global even and odd parity manifolds. c-k, Pulsed charge-stability diagrams measured for the left and right chains in the even (top) and odd (bottom) parity manifolds. Unlike conventional charge-stability diagrams referenced to the Fermi energy in a normal lead, here each chain provides the energy reference for the other. As such, the measured features reflect the difference between the excitation energies of the two individual chains. Crossings are therefore observed simultaneously for the left and right chains when the splittings of the two chains compensate each other, corresponding to the qubit degeneracy condition. Consequently, the appearance of a crossing in a single parity manifold does not imply that the corresponding chain is tuned to its sweet spot. Indeed, crossing-like features are observed in only one manifold in panels c, e, i and k. The orientation of the avoided crossings depends on the parity manifold: in the even manifold, the left and right chains exhibit the same orientation, whereas in the odd manifold the orientation is reversed, reflecting the sign difference ε12 ± ε34 between the two manifolds. Only near the sweet spot (panel g) are crossings observed for both chains in both parity manifolds simultaneously, providing a unique signature that both chains are individually tuned to their sweet spots.

Pulsed charge-stability diagrams showing p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of the right-chain gate voltages (VR1, VR2), for various values of the coupler QD pulse amplitude VC for a fixed pulse duration of 10 ns. The value of VC is indicated above each panel. The device configuration is the same as in Extended Data Fig. 8. a-h, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ 0. As VC is made more negative, the coupler QD is first brought closer to resonance and parity mixing along the degeneracy lines increases. Eventually, when the coupler QD is near or below resonance (around VC = − 9 mV), the final state is dictated by the ground state of the chain in the relevant sector of the charge-stability diagram irrespective of the initial state. We note that the chain appears to move from CAR-like at low pulse amplitudes (tR < ΔR, a) across a sweet spot (tR ≈ ΔR, b-e) to ECT-like at high pulse amplitudes (tR > ΔR, f-h), which we attribute to uncompensated cross-capacitance between VC and VRH. i-n, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ π. The main difference is that the visibility of QDR2 is suppressed, as predicted by theory (Supplementary Note 4).

p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics, corresponding to measurements shown in the main text. Unless stated otherwise, measurements are taken at VC = 9.8 mV and perpendicular field B⊥ = 15.6 mT (yellow mark in panel o), corresponding to a phase difference φ ≈ 0 between the chains. a-d, Detuning individual quantum dots. e,f, Detuning the left- (e) and right-chain QDs (f). g,h, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (g) and inner (h) QDs of both chains. i, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude. j, Varying VLH and VRH for a fixed pulse duration of 18 ns. The colored marks indicate sweep directions for panels k,l,p,q. k,l, Detuning the left (k) and right (l) chain via VLH and VRH. m, Oscillation frequency as a function of pulse amplitude in logarithmic scale, where V0 is the gate voltage at which QDC is on resonance. The gray line fits f = K/(V0 − VC) with K = 156.6 ± 0.3 MHz mV and V0 = 11.285 ± 0.002 mV for VC < 10.8 mV. n, Quality factor of the oscillations as a function of VC. o, Dependence on the out-of-plane magnetic field B⊥. p,q, Symmetric (p) and antisymmetric (q) detuning of VLH together with VRH.

p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics. Note that for this dataset, the chains were tuned using pulsed charge-stability diagrams but were not compared to the odd manifold. As such, it is unclear if the even and odd states of each chain are degenerate. a, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude VC. In contrast to the main text, QDC starts detuned below the Fermi level instead of above but is likewise pulsed closer to resonance for qubit evolution. b, Dependence on the out-of-plane magnetic field B⊥. In this case, we observe decoherence around φ = π (B⊥ ≈ 13.5 mT), consistent with a small residual detuning of an outer QD from resonance; such detuning restores transverse coupling near φ ≈ π (Supplementary Note 4). c,d, Detuning the left (c) and right (d) chain via VLH and VRH. e-h, Single-dot detuning of VL1, VL2, VR1 and VR2. i,j, Detuning the left- (i) and right-chain QDs (j). k,l, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (k) and inner (l) quantum dots of both chains.

p(eo∣eo), p(oe∣oe), p(eo∣oe), and p(oe∣eo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics, corresponding to measurements shown in the main text. a, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude VC. b,c, Detuning the left (b) and right (c) chain via VLH and VRH. d, Varying VLH and VRH for a fixed pulse duration of 18 ns. The colored marks indicate sweep directions for panels b,c,e,f. e,f, Symmetric (e) and antisymmetric (f) detuning of VLH together with VRH. g-i, Oscillation frequency (g), Rabi decay time \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) (h) and quality factor Q (i) extracted from panel a as a function of VC.

Extracted Rabi coherence time \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) for the different detuning configurations shown in Fig. 4, as indicated by the schematics. a-d, Detuning individual quantum dots. e,f, Detuning the left (e) and right (f) Kitaev chains. g,h, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (g) and inner (h) quantum dots of both chains. Gray markers indicate fits for which the relative uncertainty in \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) exceeds 50% or the fitted oscillation frequency lies outside the 10–200 MHz range, and are therefore considered unreliable. For visibility, the \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) axis is also limited to 40 ns. Fitted values beyond this range are not shown, as they also arise from unreliable fits and are not physically meaningful. The same-chain two-dot detunings show the narrowest range over which coherent oscillations can be reliably fitted, whereas the single-dot and cross-chain detunings retain resolvable oscillations over a broader range. The simultaneous two-dot detunings in panels e-h use the same voltage scales as the corresponding single-dot measurements in panels a-d, and the pulse amplitude applied to the second quantum dot is shown on the upper axis.

#1268. Erling Haaland sparks fear among fans after concerning TV interview as he admits he is 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli

Published: 04:06 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 08:33 EST, 25 November 2026

Manchester City fans have expressed concern over Erling Haaland's despondent interview following their Champions League draw with Napoli, with the star admitting he is 'questioning everything' amid their slump in form.

Enzo Maresca's side rescued a late draw at the Etihad on Tuesday night, with Rayan Cherki equalising in the 86th minute to secure a 2-2 draw with Napoli.

The result, however, continued an underwhelming run of form with Man City having won just twice in their last seven matches – one of which was achieved in a penalty shoot-out against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Man City have suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League in the run, as well as drawing with Fulham on the weekend.

Haaland, who captained Man City against Napoli, admitted post-match to TNT Sports that their underwhelming form has left the squad questioning themselves.

'We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want,' Haaland said. 'Football is easy and difficult. When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything.

Erling Haaland cut a despondent figure as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form

🗣️ "I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that there's something that's not clicking fully."@Erling reflects on @ManCity's 2-2 draw with Napoli.🎤 @AndyKerrtv #UCL | #ManCity pic.twitter.com/Cx2Hzieom3

'The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.

'We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.'

Haaland admitted in another interview with Bein Sports that the run of form 'hurts', with the star having offered a resigned laugh when asked whether the draw against Napoli should be considered a 'good point'.

The 26-year-old was seen looking down throughout the minute and a half interview, while he also rubbed his face with his hand as he looked to find answers for Man City's recent struggles.

'How the game was we managed to come back two times, but we demand more,' Haaland said.

'We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way.

'I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that it is not clicking fully and we have to find out, stay positive and get the best out of every single day.

'With and without the armband I feel huge responsibility because all I want to do is perform for this club and win games for Man City and right now we are not doing that. It hurts.'

Fans quickly noted Haaland's downbeat responses to questions and despondent body language during the interview.

Man City fans have expressed concerns over Haaland's downbeat responses and body language in the interview

Fans claimed they have never seen Haaland 'looking this flat' and suggested the star 'looks distraught' amid their underwhelming run

'I've never seen Haaland looking this flat. Not even close to it,' one commented.

'At least he’s being honest with himself. Looks distraught,' a second said, with a third writing 'Extremely concerning.'

'Never seen Erling Haaland look like this before,' another added, while a Man City fan wrote 'You can really tell how confused Haaland is from his expression. They don’t have confidence in their own football.'

One went as far as claiming 'Haaland looks like he’s done with Manchester City…' while sharing footage of his reaction to one of Napoli's goals on the night.

Other fans questioned whether Haaland and his Man City team-mates' recent slump may be related to concerns over the potential punishment the club could face for breaching financial rules.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Man City face Arsenal in a crucial match on Sunday as they look to make inroads in the Gunners six point lead at the top of the Premier League

Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

The forward's first answer to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 had spanned two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges after he was asked about the club's situation.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland said.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle…

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'

He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

The Man City star, who signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract in late 2024, told Norwegian television earlier this month that his focus was on helping the team to turn their form around.

The draw against Napoli leaves Man City lying sixth in the Champions League table - which would be enough to see Maresca's side to qualify for the last-16.

Man City face a crucial clash on the weekend when they face reigning champions Arsenal in the Premier League, as they look to halve the six-point gap to the leaders at the top of the table.

#1267. Ben Jacobs Shares Update on Liverpool Signing Lamine Camara in January

Liverpool are looking to strengthen their squad in the January transfer window, and Ben Jacobs has shared an update on their interest in bringing in a midfielder.

The Reds made three signings in the summer by bringing in Ronald Araujo, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, and the team have started the season well with the team sitting fourth in the Premier League, and having lost just three times in all competitions.

But Andoni Iraola is understood to be keen to strengthen his squad further for the second half of the season, and midfield additions are believed to be among the priority deals being targeted.

During the summer, the club were attentive to the situation regarding Lamine Camara, but a deal never materialised for them to make a move. However, GIVEMESPORT exclusively revealed that when Chelsea made a push to bring him in on Deadline Day, Liverpool made contact with the Senegal international to express their interest too.

Monaco eventually pulled the plug on his move to Stamford Bridge after the deadline had passed, refusing to put in a deal sheet, and speaking in his latest newsletter, GMS senior correspondent Ben Jacobs has now revealed that there is a chance the Reds make a move in January.

“And then just final word on Lamine Camara, like I said on deadline day exclusively, Liverpool were calling Camara on deadline day, and they were saying, 'If you don’t go to Chelsea, we could be there for you in 2027'," he said.

"And Liverpool privately, according to my information, were very glad that Camara and Chelsea fell through, and it seems like now Chelsea want Alex Scott. Unless they get a big concession on the deal, it might be difficult for Chelsea to go back to Monaco and sign Camara, because the club relationship is a bit broken because Monaco didn’t send that deal to a deal sheet.

"Chelsea were really disappointed by Monaco’s handling there, which means if they are to renegotiate for Camara and move away from Alex Scott, they would likely need Monaco to make a significant concession, and that club-to-club relationship is still very difficult.”

With lots of interest in Camara during the summer window, Monaco boss Filipe Luis was asked about his midfielder and the speculation around his future, where he admitted that he didn't want to lose him, while calling him 'one of the best midfielders in the world'.

"We are probably talking about one of the best midfielders in the world," he said.

"I don't want to talk about him too much, because I know a lot of clubs would love to have him in their squad, and he is very important to me.

"He has that quality on the ball, covers a lot of ground, he is truly top class! I am really happy to have him, and he is going to play a key role in the team.

"Keeping him? I am very hopeful he will stay. I think he is happy in Monaco. So if he stays, he can play a key role in my game plan."

With the Ligue 1 outfit currently struggling domestically this season, it's unlikely that they will want to sell mid-season. However, their financial situation means that a good offer may force their hand, and Liverpool have the cash to spend if they deem it necessary.

Chelsea are seemingly out of the race as they chase a deal for Alex Scott instead, leaving the Reds with a clear run to bring in someone they see as a top target.

#1266. Adžić undergoes surgery as Juventus loanee’s Sassuolo season may be over

Vasilije Adžić has undergone knee surgery, and the Juventus loanee could miss the rest of the season with Sassuolo.

According to a statement from Juventus, the 20-year-old Montenegro international suffered a sprain and bruising to his right knee in Montenegro’s Nations League game against Cyprus on 15 November. Tests revealed “a small osteochondral detachment”, meaning a piece of bone and cartilage had come away inside the joint.

Adžić had surgery on Thursday at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon, where Juventus captain Manuel Locatelli was also operated on in September. He has now started the rehabilitation programme “aimed at returning to competitive activity”.

Neither Juventus nor Sassuolo have given a timeframe for his recovery. However, TuttoMercatoWeb suggests the need for surgery points to a lengthy absence, with a real risk he won’t play again before the end of the 2026-27 season.

It’s a cruel blow for a player who started his loan in style. Adžić scored in three consecutive Serie A games in September, including a curling winner off the bench in Sassuolo’s 3-2 victory over Juventus. His form has tailed off since then, and he has three goals and one assist in nine league appearances.

The injury could also affect his future. Sassuolo paid €500,000 to take him on loan in the summer and included an option to buy fixed at €12m, while Juventus kept a buy-back clause. A long spell out leaves both clubs with little to go on when they decide his future next summer.

It's been ten months since Brooklyn Beckham launched an explosive attack on his parents, and despite this very public feud, the son of the Manchester United legend appears to be doing very well.

Accusing his mother, Victoria, of 'sabotaging' his wedding to his spouse Nicola Peltz, Brooklyn also criticised the artificial nature of the 'Beckham Brand'.

Distancing himself from his loved ones, Beckham's eldest child has gone in a completely different direction, settling with Peltz in Beverly Hills, Los Angeles.

Despite no longer holding ties to his family, Brooklyn is seemingly still living a lush lifestyle with his wife and children.

Brooklyn spent this year's Thanksgiving with his beloved wife, Peltz, and six other guests at the couple's home in Beverly Hills.

The aspiring chef forked out a reported £130 on a piece of cheese from 'the Cheese Store of Beverly Hills' (via the Mirror). The store shared a video on their social media pages, which revealed how Brooklyn splashed the cash.

In the clip, the model was captured informing the Cheese store's owner how much he enjoys watching their cheese videos in bed whilst his wife watches make-up tutorials.

Brooklyn's love for cooking is well-documented, and he admitted earlier this week that he was apprehensive about preparing a big Thanksgiving spread.

Victoria is said to be "devastated" by the claims made by her eldest son as sources recount what happened on Brooklyn's well-documented wedding day.

In the cheese store, the former Arsenal academy star revealed that he would be brining his turkey in Guinness, whilst he also detailed his plans to wake up early and slow-cook the meat in the oven, before presenting it alongside a dish of sweet potato and marshmallows.

This was his first Thanksgiving away from his parents and siblings, instead spending the American holiday with his American wife and children, who celebrate the festivity annually.

"It must be like a dagger to the heart for David, who is so desperate to see his son. Watching Brooklyn beam alongside a man David fell out with so publicly, treating him like a mentor, would be enough to crush any father."

Back in January, Brooklyn released an explosive statement via social media, detailing his relationship with his family. In the statement, he explained that he had no plans to reconcile with his parents after they'd 'controlled narratives' in the press throughout his life.

"I have been silent for years and made every effort to keep these matters private," the statement read.

"Unfortunately, my parents and their team have continued to go to the press, leaving me with no choice but to speak for myself and tell the truth about only some of the lies that have been printed.

"I do not want to reconcile with my family. I'm not being controlled, I'm standing up for myself for the first time in my life. For my entire life, my parents have controlled narratives in the press about our family. "Recently, I have seen with my own eyes the lengths that they'll go through to place countless lies in the media, mostly at the expense of innocent people, to preserve their own facade. But I believe the truth always comes out. My parents have been trying endlessly to ruin my relationship since before my wedding, and it hasn't stopped.

"My mum cancelled making Nicola's dress in the eleventh hour despite how excited she was to wear her design, forcing her to urgently find a new dress. Weeks before our big day, my parents repeatedly pressured and attempted to bribe me into signing away the rights to my name, which would have affected me, my wife, and our future children.

"They were adamant on me signing before my wedding date because then the terms of the deal would be initiated. My holdout affected the payday, and they have never treated me the same since.

"During the wedding planning, my mum went so far as to call me 'evil' because Nicola and I chose to include my Nanny Sandra, and Nicola's Naunni, at our table, because they both didn't have their husbands. Both of our parents had their own tables equally adjacent to ours. The night before our wedding, members of my family told me that Nicola was 'not blood' and 'not family.'

"Since the moment I started standing up for myself with my family, I've received endless attacks from my parents, both privately and publicly, that were sent to the press on their orders. Even my brothers were sent to attack me on social media, before they ultimately blocked me out of nowhere this last summer.

"My mum hijacked my first dance with my wife, which had been planned weeks in advance to a romantic love song. In front of our 500 wedding guests, Marc Anthony called me to the stage, where in the schedule was planned to be my romantic dance with my wife, but instead my mum was waiting to dance with me instead. She danced very inappropriately on me in front of everyone.

A guest in attendance has now spoken out amid allegations over Victoria Beckham's dancing.

"I've never felt more uncomfortable or humiliated in my entire life. We wanted to renew our vows so we could create new memories of our wedding day that bring us joy and happiness, not anxiety and embarrassment.

Conor Coady has emerged as one of the candidates to become new head coach at Blackpool.

He is keen to make the step up in club coaching and was linked with a role at Barnsley in recent weeks.

#1263. What Bruno Fernandes’ new Manchester United contract means for Milan

Manchester United have triggered a one-year extension on Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ending Milan’s hopes of signing him on a free transfer next summer.

According to The Athletic, the club captain is now tied to Old Trafford until June 2028. Fernandes had been entering the final year of his deal and recently confirmed that talks over a new contract had been put on hold, with both sides wanting to focus on improving results.

By exercising the option, United have stopped the 32-year-old from negotiating with foreign clubs from 1 January, when he would otherwise have been free to agree a pre-contract.

That doesn’t rule out a move next year, but any club wanting Fernandes will now have to pay a fee. Milan are among the European clubs monitoring him, along with interest from Saudi Arabia, and United have already identified possible replacements.

The Portuguese midfielder’s future had looked uncertain after Michael Carrick dropped him for a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth. That followed his public criticism of the team’s tactics after a 4-1 Champions League loss to Como.

Since then, however, Fernandes has kept the captaincy under new coach Mauricio Pochettino and scored twice in Wednesday’s 2-2 draw at Sporting CP.

#1262. Lee Carsley Confirms his Stance on Tottenham and England U21 Star Archie Gray

England U21s manager Lee Carsley shared his thoughts on Archie Gray with GIVEMESPORT, as the Tottenham midfielder approaches a vital decision about his international career.

Carsley has been busy preparing for next summer's European Championship, as he looks to secure silverware for the third time in charge of the U21s.

The task ahead has now become even clearer following the official draw. The young Three Lions will square off against France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia in Group A in what Carsley hopes will hand his side a routine entry into the knockout stage.

Just who will be involved in Carsley's squad is now the big question. European football is scattered with top English talents these days and the U21s boss is expected to take full advantage of that.

Carsley spoke to GIVEMESPORT following the draw in Belgrade on Thursday, having his say on several young stars in the process.

The 52-year-old took the opportunity to speak about the likes of Manchester United youngster Ayden Heaven, as well as Gray, who has a particularly important decision to make in the near future.

The versatile Tottenham star has represented England from U15 to U21 level, but is yet to receive a senior call-up. As long as that is the case, the rules dictate that he will be allowed to represent another national team at senior level as long as he is eligible.

England's 20 best players right now have been ranked, including Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka.

That should offer Scotland some hope. Gray is eligible to play for England's rivals through his father, Andy Gray, who made two appearances for Scotland, his grandfather Frank Gray, who was a European champion with Nottingham Forest and became a star defender with Scotland, and great-uncle Eddie Gray, who also played in front of the Tartan Army.

It's certainly a predicament for the 20-year-old, but he's already had a conversation about his potential England future with Carsley.

"Archie, like a lot of the players, is important to the Under-21s. He’s got a fantastic history in the pathway, a player that we really enjoy working with. There’s no change to what we spoke about previously."

The England U21s boss kept his cards close to his chest when it came to the details of that conversation, but Gray is certainly someone that he rates.

Whether Thomas Tuchel feels the same way remains to be seen. If the Three Lions are to turn the Spurs man into a fully-fledged England international, then they may have to do so sooner rather than later.

It's not just Carsley who's had his say on Gray's international career. The midfielder, himself, has also commented. He admitted back in 2024 that his desire is to represent England in a major blow for Scotland.

He told reporters: "My hopes are to play for England, definitely. It’s where I’m from and where I’ve grown up. I’m three quarters English, so that’s where’ I’m at. My dad is totally happy for whatever makes me happy, even though Eddie supports Scotland. But I’m the same as him, I’m happy as long as he’s happy.

"Hopefully I can (get England recognition), but I’ve just got to take it step by step and keep focusing on my club football, which can hopefully attract the attention of whoever it is, whether it’s the Under-21s or it’s the first team. I’d be really happy just to play for my country."

Whether that lasts the test of time if Gray fails to earn a senior England call-up is the big unanswered question, however. He certainly wouldn't be the first player to switch allegiances.

Lee Carsley speaks on Jobe Bellingham, Max Dowman, England, and more, in a conversation with GIVEMESPORT.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.
