#1261. James Penrice warns Rangers they must improve if they intend to hit the Scottish Premiership summit

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 10:26 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 10:37 EST, 25 November 2026

James Penrice has warned that Rangers can forget about going top of the table on Saturday if they play like they did for the first 45 minutes against Aberdeen.

Derek McInnes’ side were a goal down at half-time and heading to their first defeat in 14 games after failing to get going against the Dons.

With the manager making three changes at half-time, the Ibrox men scored three times in an incredible 11-minute burst through Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

And while Aberdeen netted again via Findlay Marshall, Rangers hung on for the win which put them within a point of Celtic.

With the leaders facing Hearts at Tynecastle on Sunday, McInnes’ men can move to the summit if they defeat high-flying Falkirk the day before. But Penrice says that will only happen if they deliver a more complete display than they showed on Tuesday.

‘It’s a massive incentive for us, but the league isn’t won in November,’ said the defender. ‘Falkirk are playing well. They’ve travelled well away from home too.

James Penrice has warned Rangers they will need to improve if they are to take top spot

‘We’ll need to be on it. We can’t go into that game like we did on Tuesday night. I wouldn’t say we were lucky, but we can’t concede two goals at home. We can’t do that on Saturday.

‘Is it important we grab that chance (to go top)? Definitely. We’ll just concentrate on ourselves. It’s another game to tick off and we’ll turn up hoping to get the three points.’

McInnes introduced Tuur Rommens, Findlay Curtis and Kim Min-su at the break with the changes leading to a much-improved display.

Despite chalking up the win which maintained the unbeaten run, Penrice insists the overall show left considerable room for improvement.

‘It was very mixed,’ he reflected. ‘We concede in the first half, but then fly out the traps in the second.

‘I thought we were really good for 20 minutes. We go and score a third and look comfortable. But then we switch off. We turned our back at a free-kick and they end up scoring. We made it difficult for ourselves.

‘But we got three goals. Ryan got his usual one where he’s alive in the box. Gas was brilliant and he got his goal then Nico got his. But again, we made it hard for ourselves. The main thing is we got three points.

‘We made a few changes at half-time and I thought the boys who came on were brilliant. They had that real spark and energy. We started the second half really well but, ultimately, we need to score more.

Rangers goalscorers Djeidi Gassama, Nico Raskin and Ryan Naderi celebrate against Aberdeen

‘We could have done that and made it easy for ourselves.’

Rangers haven’t now tasted defeat since losing away to Czech side Jablonec on August 27. And while not every display in that run has been outstanding, Penrice is encouraged by the fact that the team is showing plenty of character.

‘We’ve shown we’ve got a bit of resilience,’ he said. ‘It’s not a bad trait to be winning games and scoring late on. We’re doing that. But as players we want to make the game as easy as possible.

‘We’re on a run just now and hopefully it continues.

‘The positives on Tuesday night were that, in spells, we were really good. We were flying in the second half. But we can’t concede two goals at home and expect to always come away with a win.’

Meanwhile, Penrice says he’s got no fears that Min-su will become a goal threat for the team.

The South Korean, an £8.5million summer signing from Girona, has yet to find the net in 14 appearances with his sole assist coming against Motherwell last Saturday.

The forward thought he’d broken his duck with a spectacular late effort against the Dons only for the ball to sail over.

‘I said to Min-su at full-time that me and big Ryan were ready to run to him at 100mph if he’d scored that goal,’ Penrice smiled.

‘You can see he wants it so bad. He probably just needs to calm down in front of goal.

‘I thought that was the one when he chopped inside. I thought he was scoring, but he put it into row Z.

Kim Min-su has impressed for Rangers but is still waiting to score his first goal for the club

‘It wasn’t ideal, but he was still happy afterward because we won the game.

‘You can see in his game that, at every opportunity, he’s trying to get a shot away. It will come and hopefully it comes at a perfect time.

‘There’s a reason these players are at Ibrox — it’s because they’re extremely talented. It’s just that last bit but they’re very young.

‘Min-su’s game isn’t just goals and assists. He’s a really talented footballer who creates problems for teams. He’s been a massive part of why we’re on this run. You can all see it.

‘It’s about more than goals and assists, but if he adds that to his game, he’s only going to go on and have a very successful career.

‘That’s what the boys want for him. We want our wide players and strikers to score as many as possible.’

#1260. Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

This was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

Robin Roefs is at it again with another important save for Sunderland 👏 https://t.co/SJ4qWmSHBo

Had the former Newcastle United player scored so late in the game, the home crowd’s frustration may have boiled over. The point means Le Bris’ side have still not won a league game since August and remain bottom of the table. This is proving to be a tougher second season in the top flight for Sunderland, but if they keep playing like this, they will not remain in the bottom three for much longer.

“It’s a positive [point],” said Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it’s a new challenge for us and we need to embrace it. I think we showed this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today.”

Sunderland were warned about “second season syndrome” and shrugged them off in the summer as they looked forward to their first European campaign for more than 50 years.

They had dismissed the gloomy pre-season predictions the previous year and had gone on to enjoy their most successful season in the top flight since the heady days of the Peter Reid era at the start of the century.

So when the “experts” told them it would be much harder this season—that they would no longer have the element of surprise and the squad would be badly stretched by the extra games in the Europa League—it was easy to ignore.

You cannot blame them. It has been a magical couple of years on Wearside where everything has gone in their favour, but reality has hit hard this season.

Sunderland are bottom of the table heading into this home game against Leeds United and have not won in the league since August.

The limp defeat at Bournemouth last weekend brought things to a head, with defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting in a post match interview that his teammates had become arrogant and had forgotten how hard they had to work last season to be successful.

There was a better performance and a decent draw away to Lech Poznan on Thursday night but Regis Le Bris’ side desperately need a win in the league.

Leeds United have been one of the story’s of the season so far and have looked dangerous in every game so far.

The return to fitness of Brian Brobbey is a big boost for Sunderland, but I don’t think any side would like to face Leeds at the moment. The home crowd will be anxious.

Régis Le Bris has made three changes to his Sunderland side.

Brian Brobbey returns to the starting line-up after recovering from a hamstring injury, while Luke O’Nien and Nilson Angulo also come into the side.

Omar Alderete and Timur Tutierov are named among the substitutes, while Kevin Danso begins a one-match suspension following his red card at Bournemouth.

Manager Daniel Farke has made three changes to his starting line-up.

Jaka Bijol replaces Nico Elvedi and starts alongside Tarik Muharemovic and James Justin. Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson both start in place of Anton Stach and Noah Okafor, supporting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the Leeds United attack.

Leeds United: Trafford, Justin, Bijol, Muharemović, Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson, Wilson, Aaronson, Calvert-LewinSubs: Zetterer, Bard, Longstaff, Stach, Gruev, Cresswell, Nmecha, Okafor, Bahoya

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light.

The final game of this gameweek sees these two Northern giants lock horns once again in a very intriguing encounter, with Sunderland especially in need of three points.

Following their opening season back in the Premier League last term, Sunderland enjoyed a historic campaign, placing seventh to qualify for European competition for the first time in 53 years. Therefore, their workload for the 2025-26 season has increased, which has caused their domestic form to suffer.

Sunderland currently find themselves bottom of the top-flight table, with just one win and four points from their opening seven league matches. They’ve lost their previous four Premier League games, but a win here could lift them out of the drop zone, depending on other results at Old Trafford and Selhurst Park.

Meanwhile, in the Europa League, it’s a completely different story. Regis Le Bris’ side are unbeaten, earning seven points from the first nine available. They drew 1-1 with Polish outfit Lech Poznan on Thursday evening, and given the relentless juggling act of domestic and European football, they’re already back in today against a very well-drilled team.

Leeds have made a solid start to the season and find themselves eighth in the Premier League, having only lost one match — a narrow 2-1 defeat to Arsenal at the Emirates earlier this month. Last time out, Daniel Farke’s side drew 1-1 with Manchester United at Elland Road, meaning they’re still searching for a first Premier League win since September 14.

Speaking in his preview, Farke said: “To win any point in this league, you always have to be on it. And you always have to be close to be perfect, especially for normal sides - not like the top two. And for that, we are very respectful. So we don’t go into the trap and think we are bigger than we are. We are just the second year back on Premier League level. And we fight for every point.”

#1259. Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

#1258. England U21s boss Lee Carsley Shares his True Feelings on Max Dowman

England U21s boss Lee Carsley has delivered his verdict on the young stars who are continuing to make waves in the Premier League.

The 52-year-old is actively preparing to defend England's crown at next summer's European Championship, which he is looking to win for the third time in his managerial career at youth level.

The Three Lions have the chance to pick up their third-consecutive victory, having also secured silverware in 2023 and 2025, and could become the first side to do so since Italy between 1992 and 1996.

Simply put, the talent in Carsley's hands is historic and he is well aware of that. The coach took time to praise several England stars ahead of the official draw, which saw the Three Lions placed in Group A with Poland, France, and co-hosts Serbia.

Carsley had the chance to speak highly of Archie Gray, who has a big decision to make about the future of his international career, and Arsenal's Max Dowman.

The latter has become the centre of conversation in English football since he became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history against Everton last season. Many believe he will be the future of Thomas Tuchel's side.

Carsley decided to join in with the praise on Thursday evening, telling GIVEMESPORT: "I think he showed last camp that he was more than capable of being there. He’s an outstanding talent on and off the pitch.

"Great player to work with. Lovely kid as well also, which is really important. Settled into the group nicely. Max is a player that we rate highly."

Arsenal legend David Seaman has named a 'special' star as his surprise pick for the England Euro 2028 squad.

Having already secured a record in the Premier League, Dowman also still has the chance to become a history-maker at international level.

If the 16-year-old earns his first senior England cap in the next 12 months, then he will become the youngest player in the country's history to play for the Three Lions - beating Theo Walcott, who was 17 years and 75 days old when he debuted in 2006.

If this current England generation is golden, then the next looks like it could be pure platinum. England's next best stars are quickly making a name for themselves around European and English football.

Luca Williams-Barnett is now well on his way to stardom at Tottenham. Rio Ngumoha is already arguably Liverpool's most dangerous wide man and is already a stat-leader in the Champions League - completing more take-ons than anyone else.

Then there's Dowman, who's just waiting to become Arsenal's difference-maker when the time is right. All three stars have received high praise, with former Premier League forward Jay Bothroyd going as far as dubbing Dowman "the future of England".

While there will be plenty of focus on the U21s Euros next summer, there are already several stars who are ready to make their mark for the senior side. And when the 2028 senior European Championship arrives, they may do exactly that.

England's 20 best players right now have been ranked, including Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka.

#1257. Report: Lookman price tag set by Atletico as Roma monitor closely

Atlético Madrid are prepared to sell Ademola Lookman in January, less than a year after signing him from Atalanta.

According to Spanish outlet Fichajes, via CalcioMercato, the Nigerian forward is no longer considered untouchable by Diego Simeone, and the club would listen to offers. They won’t let him go cheaply, though. Atlético want a permanent sale worth at least the €35-40m they paid Atalanta last February.

Lookman is currently sidelined with a knee sprain picked up on international duty with Nigeria. The Super Eagles’ staff initially thought it was minor, but tests in Madrid showed a more serious problem, although the ligaments don’t appear to be involved. He is expected to be out until early 2027, which means he should return just as the January window opens.

Inter were previously strong admirers, but they now plan to spend their January budget on defence. That leaves Roma as the most likely Serie A destination.

Gian Piero Gasperini turned Lookman into one of Europe’s most dangerous forwards at Atalanta, despite their well-documented clashes over transfers. The Roma coach has been looking for a player with his profile since the summer.

Roma also have a good relationship with Atlético, having already done business with them over Nahuel Molina.

#1256. Raheem Sterling's chaotic descent is a product of the cocooned world where football's little princes can't handle rejection, writes IAN HERBERT - now he must listen to those around him if he wants to salvage his career

By IAN HERBERT - DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 08:21 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 25 November 2026

Raheem Sterling wore black to his sentencing hearing today, just as he had when he arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates Court two months ago and admitted to 90 minutes of terrifying rush hour driving, with canisters of nitrous oxide on the passenger seat beside him.

He was visibly more subdued this time, wearing the look of a man who’d spent two months contemplating the prospect of a jail stretch, whilst the contemporaries he once stood with in the England squad, Harry Kane, Jordan Henderson and Jordan Pickford, were continuing to hit the heights.

Imprisonment was only ever a narrow possibility under the sentencing guidelines for dangerous driving, given the miracle that Sterling did not cause serious injury or worse as he zig-zagged between lanes on the M3 and M4 that morning last May. Critically, he was not found to be under the influence of nitrous oxide. A motorist who drove in equally erratic fashion and initially ignored police on Cheshire’s M56, in a BMW which had only three tyres, was handed a suspended sentence earlier this year.

But while the mitigation preceding the magistrate’s decision that Sterling would walk free - his 12-month prison sentence is suspended for 18 months - garlanded him for his charity work and promotion of racial equality, don’t let it be said that his conduct that day was anything less than a disgrace. The tetchy hyper sensitivity Sterling displayed with the police officers who arrested him revealed a shocking lack of contrition and shame.

Sterling has had his challenges, of course. The early death of his father and a nomadic London childhood spent helping his mum on cleaning jobs. But then he disappeared into the cocooned existence of the football academy world, full of the little princes who have people fawning over them, telling them how good they are and throwing obscene amounts of money at them.

Raheem Sterling's conduct the day of his car crash was nothing short of a disgrace

Sterling's meteoric rise has meant he does not have the tools to deal with rejection

Kane has flourished in a way that Sterling hasn’t because he was forced to learn the hard way, deal with rejection and develop a sense of perspective. The princes are at the mercy of the hangers on and leeches, around them for a cut of their next big pay cheque. It was Sterling’s misfortune to select Aidy Ward as his agent – the man who conducted ugly, public contract negotiations with Liverpool which included declaring that Sterling wouldn’t be staying at Anfield even if he were offered nearly £1m a week. The reputational damage that caused Sterling should have seen him sack Ward on the spot.

The problem for those whose adolescence takes place in football’s gilded cage is that they combust and can’t hack it when the going gets remotely tough. For Sterling, read Dele Alli, Kalvin Phillips and Aaron Ramsdale.

But what makes Sterling’s personal disintegration so needless is that he really has had positive influences around him in the background. Friends who were there when he wanted to develop a voice to speak against racial discrimination in football. There when he wanted to establish a Foundation to help the kind of London teenagers that he used to be.

He lost those influences during the chaotic descent into the insanity of that spring morning when he went berserk in his car. Some of them have described to me how he flatly refused to respond to calls and went into ‘oblivion mode’ in the hours after his arrest. It seemed like he was seeking escape from any vestige of the game which is all he has known.

England captain and Sterling's former team-mate Harry Kane has thrived due to the early setbacks in his career

The tragedy is Sterling has a strong support network who want the best for him

The bleak reality for Sterling is that his career in football is surely over now. Yes, he could pick up the thread in some place below the Premier League, though his unhappy experience at Feyenoord – where there was a prurient fascination with his struggles – suggests that he will face the same relentless scrutiny wherever he goes. In the modern world, more gratuitous pleasure than ever is taken in the fall of those who were once great. It will be a circus if he pitches up somewhere new.

But the evidence of that work with boys in London suggests that he has far more of a hinterland to turn to than Alli and his ilk, if only he can re-establish those positive influences and seek help.

A moment in time, precisely two years ago, proves what his future might look like. At a meeting room in King's Cross, Sterling sat with a group of seven young men, all of whom were deemed at risk of drifting into knife crime and who had been sent along to his foundation by Brent's youth offending service.

After an initial 15 or 20 minutes when the boys seemed blinded by the superstar in their midst, they became more comfortable, seeming to feel he understood the likes of them. There were smiles as he described the various school social groups he knew. 'The cool group, the middle of the road group and the geeks,' as he called them. The 'geeks' always seemed to be a bigger part of his world when exams approached, he said with a grin. The room was wreathed with laughter, then.

The group session evolved into several one-to-one conversations between him and the boys who'd been more reticent. It was then that he pointed out the value of allowing outside mentors to help you, if your home life is challenging. 'Having someone else involved changed the course of my life,' Sterling told them.

Now is the moment when Sterling needs others to help change the course of his own life and if he accepts that, he could play a part in public life again. First comes the challenge of rousing himself from any lingering self-pity, emerging from the celebrity bubble and appreciating that he is supremely lucky to remain a free man after those abominable, mindless few hours in his souped-up car.

#1255. Chelsea Fans Slam ‘Pathetic’ Cole Palmer After Loss vs Forest

Chelsea slumped to yet another defeat on Friday night, this time at the hands of Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, and Blues fans aren't best pleased with one player in particular.

The West Londoners fell behind after just five minutes when Igor Jesus spectacularly volleyed past Emi Martinez after excellent work from Daniel Munoz down the right. Xabi Alonso's team mustered up just two shots in what was a dire opening 45 minutes from the away side.

Forest doubled their advantage shortly after the break when Morgan Gibbs-White sent Martinez the wrong way from 12 yards after Wesley Fofana had clumsily brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea penalty area. The Blues hit back minutes later, with substitute Emanuel Emegha on hand to pounce on a loose ball and slot beyond Matz Sels.

The home team restored their two-goal cushion with 18 minutes left to play, when Gibbs-White added to his tally by clipping the ball over the on-rushing Martinez after Xaver Schlager's exquisite through ball. Emegha pulled one back late on with a neat header, but it wasn't enough for Alonso's men.

The result sees Forest move away from the relegation zone and up into 14th, while Chelsea remain eighth, five points behind Liverpool in fourth.

Alonso's outfit are on a dismal run, losing each of their last three Premier League matches, and fans are subsequently growing frustrated.

While there have been a few murmurings around the manager's future, the focus of Blues supporters' discontent has largely centred around the players.

Fofana, who conceded the penalty that gifted Forest a second goal, was the subject of hostility from the travelling crowd, who booed the Frenchman whilst he was in possession.

However, online, Chelsea fans took aim at a different player. Palmer, who created just one chance and took no shots on the night, was heavily scrutinised by his own supporters on social media.

One fan bluntly wrote on X: "Cole Palmer. What a waste of space."

"Cole Palmer has actually fallen off a cliff, what am I watching here?" another added.

Meanwhile, one fan had a team selection suggestion for Alonso, urging him to drop Palmer for the next game and start Estevao instead.

"Palmer needs to be benched for a game at this point. Let Estevao fight for his spot."

"What happened to Palmer? He looks to have lost his attacking prowess," another wrote.

This theme continued, with another fan stating that the playmaker is 'a shadow of himself' and another accusing the player of 'ghosting again'.

The Blues have slipped into eighth in the Premier League following a 4-1 home rout.

Meanwhile, two more roped Morgan Rogers into the criticism.

"Rogers & Palmer, I have no words for you both," one posited.

Finally, a supporter described the pair's displays as 'pathetic': "Palmer and Rogers have been pathetic."

What makes Palmer special when he's performing at his best level is his ability to create chances and get shots off from difficult positions. Against Forest, he did neither.

He played within himself, opting against risky moves in the final third and instead choosing to retain possession. Creating one chance, taking no shots and completing just two dribbles, it was a completely ineffective performance from the number ten.

Alonso has tasked the England international with dropping deep from time to time to help Chelsea progress the ball. He did this relatively well at the City Ground, completing nine line-breaking passes, but this came at the expense of his influence in the final third.

While Palmer must step up and take more responsibility, his coach needs to concoct a system that elicits more from his star attacker.

#1254. REVEALED: Full story of Amar Dedic's bow and arrows fiasco including helicopter search, Saudi sale talk truth as new stadium edges closer and first images of stunning private members' club at new £190m training base - Newcastle Confidential

Published: 12:00 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 25 November 2026

Newcastle chiefs are inching closer to confirming a new stadium as their direction of travel.

We reported in last week’s Newcastle Confidential how advanced talks with New York investment bankers Goldman Sachs over financing the £1.3billion project had indicated significant progress on the decision to leave St James’ Park, with a 65,000-capacity stadium on nearby Leazes Park the intention.

Fellow Wall Street firm JP Morgan have now been appointed as advisers in selling a stake in the club, and this would be to inject new equity to help fund infrastructural developments, including a stadium.

Sources have stressed this is not a case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund looking to sell the club, but rather by creating new shares – potentially worth up to 25 per cent of the club – it raises capital for such a significant outlay.

With Newcastle said to be valued at £1.5billion, this could equate to a £375million cash injection. PIF would retain their majority ownership, even if diluted to around 63 per cent from its current 85 per cent holding.

As one source said: ‘This is not about taking cash off the table, it is about funding growth.'

Yasir Al-Rummayan and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund are not looking to sell Newcastle despite their plans to sell a stake in the club

We understand Goldman Sachs are still involved, and their role will be to provide a loan or other investment to help finance the stadium. As we reported last week, the cost of a new home would not be exclusively funded by PIF and co-owner Jamie Reuben, with loans, share issues and investments all part of the package.

The expectation is that a new stadium, rather than a St James’ renovation, will soon be recommended to the club’s owners by the executive team. It will then be up to PIF to sign off on the plans and for a public announcement to be prepared.

REVEALED: What Dedic was doing in bow and arrow fiasco!

Amar Dedic was firing arrows at a tree during his infamous countryside escapade, Confidential can now reveal.

The details of exactly what the Newcastle defender was doing with a bow and arrows in a Northumberland beauty spot can be shared for the first time after police closed the case, including the deployment of a helicopter to track him down.

The chopper was part of a major search operation in which Dedic and his friend were stopped by more than half a dozen patrol cars.

Investigators are now satisfied the 24-year-old posed no threat to the public after a 999 caller reported seeing two men walking by a reservoir with what they described as a ‘crossbow’. It was, in fact, a bow and arrows.

I can reveal that Dedic was not hunting animals (or the public) during his Harlow Hill adventure, but was instead using a tree for target practice. He and his pal were firing beyond a fence with the aim of landing their arrows in the trunk.

However, while the recreational archers were walking back to Dedic’s car, the emergency call was made by a concerned member of the public. Police cars, including armed response, arrived on the scene but the Bosnian had left.

Amar Dedic was firing arrows at a tree during his infamous countryside escapade, which saw police despatch a helicopter to track him down

Dedic has taken the misunderstanding in good spirits, and we can expect him to copy Harvey Barnes' archer celebration if he scores in the coming weeks

This prompted controllers at Northumbria Police HQ to scramble a helicopter to join the hunt and, seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate, Dedic was pulled over amid a blaze of blue lights.

Adding to the incredulity of the situation was the sudden appearance of goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett, who helped Dedic and police during questioning. They were in the area by chance.

Dedic has taken the misunderstanding in good spirits and, if he does score his first goal for Newcastle in the coming weeks, we should expect a Harvey Barnes-style archer celebration.

Joelinton is set to return to action next week – in time for the Tyne-Wear derby.

Confidential reported last week that the prognosis was not as bad as first feared after the Brazilian suffered a muscle injury during the defeat by Everton on November 2. However, I’m now told Joelinton is expected to return to full training next week, with Manchester United the visitors on Wednesday followed by the clash with Sunderland four days later.

The 30-year-old started three league games after a previous injury absence before he broke down again, raising serious questions over his ability to withstand a Premier League season. Nonetheless, Joelinton’s involvement for the derby would be a major boost to Matthias Jaissle in his first taste of the fixture.

First images of Toon's luxury private members' club

Newcastle have taken inspiration from NFL giants Dallas Cowboys as they explore plans for a luxury private members' club at their £190million training headquarters – and I can reveal stunning images of how the exclusive facility would look.

Confidential understands club chiefs have been studying some of the world's leading sporting complexes, including The Star, the Cowboys' spectacular training base in Texas, as they look to transform their own 260-acre site into a world-class destination.

And their ambitions could extend well beyond football. Newcastle have now approached existing hospitality clients and members of their business club to gauge interest in a private members' retreat within the proposed training complex at Woolsington, which is set to open in the summer of 2029.

We can reveal the first concept images of a private members' club at Newcastle's proposed £190m training base

The Dallas Cowboys' HQ in Frisco, Texas is one source of inspiration for the envisaged facility at Woolsington (pictured)

The market research includes questions about whether prospective members would be interested in business meeting spaces, a licensed bar and leisure club facilities. The idea is to create an exclusive social and business hub alongside the new training ground, which will house the men's first team and academy, with further plans to integrate the women's team.

The Dallas Cowboys' headquarters in Frisco, Texas, has provided one source of inspiration. Known as The Star, the sprawling development combines elite training facilities with hospitality, entertainment, restaurants and commercial spaces. Club officials have visited NFL facilities as part of extensive research into how the world's leading sports organisations operate away from matchdays.

The striking concept images that we are able to bring you offer a glimpse of the scale of Newcastle's ambition as they seek to build a complex that will rank as one of the best in world football.

Sporting director Ross Wilson has a new neighbour – Matthias Jaissle!

The pair are now living in the same complex in the Jesmond area of Newcastle, after Jaissle spent an initial period staying in the Dakota Hotel on the city’s Quayside.

This should prove handy ahead of the January window, and the club’s transfer war room might well become Wilson’s living room!

The car park also offers a clue as to what time Jaissle is starting work every day, and given Wilson rarely sees the manager’s vehicle there in the morning, it is assumed he is at the club’s Benton base before the milkman!

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is out of the Dakota Hotel, having moved into the same complex as the club's sporting director Ross Wilson

Finally, Newcastle have beaten Sunderland on Tyneside, 16 years after their last league victory!

Two teams of legends played a game of walking football at Newcastle’s Foundation building close to St James’ Park on Wednesday.

And we can reveal that Newcastle won 14-3! The Toon team included Shay Given, Olivier Bernard, Steve Howey, Shola Ameobi, Dummett, John Anderson and Kenny Wharton. The top scorers, surprisingly, were said to be former left backs Bernard and Dummett!

The get-together was aimed at raising awareness over walking football opportunities, with the Newcastle Foundation and Sunderland’s Foundation of Light both supporting the sport through various initiatives.

#1252. Zlatan Ibrahimovic Named His ‘Most Talented’ Teammate Ever - Snubbed Messi and Rooney

Truth be told, if Zlatan Ibrahimovic could name himself as his most talented ever teammate, then he probably would. Unfortunately for him, though, that's not how it tends to work.

Whether the Swede will ever admit it or not, he had the chance to play with some generational stars throughout an illustrious career. He spent time at AC Milan, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona, Ajax, Inter Milan and Manchester United - making an impact wherever he went.

By the end of his career, Ibrahimavic had more than 500 goals to his name. Wherever he went, he was the star of the show. But every show needs co-stars and the towering striker had those in abundance.

It's not often that an inflated ego is justifiable, but when you've had the career that Ibrahimovic had, then perhaps it's fair to refer to yourself in third person.

The former Barcelona man linked up with some undeniable legends throughout his time on the pitch, too. At the Nou Camp, he was flanked by Lionel Messi - argaubly the greatest player of all time. Even he didn't deny Messi's GOAT status during punditry duty at the 2026 World Cup.

"We spend years comparing him to everyone else, but even the greats before him can’t match the complete body of work. Pele, [Diego] Maradona, [Johan] Cruyff, whoever you want to name, they were all brilliant, but Messi’s numbers, longevity, and trophies put him in a category of his own."

In the latter stages of his career, Ibrahimovic had the chance to play with Wayne Rooney at Man United. It wasn't exactly the Red Devils at the peak of their powers, but the duo still gave Old Trafford a taste of what life may have looked like with both in the prime of their careers.

At AC Milan, the iconic forward also played with Andrea Pirlo, who was so often a striker's dream throughout his career. The list could go on and on, but none of Ibrahimovic's former teammates are more talented than one special South American, according to the Swede himself.

It takes a lot to snub the likes of Messi and Rooney, but to Ibrahimovic's defence, he has quite the list of teammates to pick from. When he was asked to narrow that list down to one name, he selected Brazilian star Adriano.

Having played with the Brazilian at Inter from 2006 to 2009, Adriano and Ibrahimovic had the chance to form quite the partnership. Their best season came in the 08/09 campaign when the duo scored a combined 55 goals as Inter picked up a fourth-straight Serie A title.

While mental health battles prevented the Brazilian from ever truly reaching his full potential, Adriano remains the "most talented" teammate that Ibrahimovic has ever had.

Speaking to reporters, Ibrahimovic spoke highly of the former Inter man, saying: "I played with great champions. I played with players that were already...wow. I played with players that I saw were a talent and became...wow.

"But the one I felt could [play at the top for] longer, and he didn't do it, was Adriano when I was at Inter. When I came to Inter the first thing I said to the president was 'I demand [Adriano] to stay because he is the player I want to play with'.

"Because, the way he was, he was an animal. He could shoot from every angle. Nobody could tackle him, nobody could take the ball, he was a pure animal. But, it last for a short time."

Adriano is a Brazilian cult hero who had the world at his feet in the mid-2000s. It's fair to say his life has been a rollercoaster ride.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1251. Chelsea Confidential: Meet Sebas Parrilla, the fiery, marathon-running, Bruce Springsteen fan Xabi Alonso trusts above all others - and why he's the man to fix Blues' defensive crisis

Published: 12:00 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 25 November 2026

Xabi Alonso is not alone in trying to halt Chelsea’s lurch into crisis. He is surrounded by a small army of staff. Some may be familiar to you, others less so.

There is Willie Isa, the ‘cultural architect’ preparing the defenders for headed duels by acting as a human shield in training drills.

There is Andre Reis, the new set-piece analyst studying Nottingham Forest’s approach to corners so Austin MacPhee can formulate instructions for the team.

There is Simon Morris and Stu Sullivan, the sports massage therapists preparing the players for their Friday night turnaround. And so on.

But the voice Alonso trusts most at Chelsea belongs to Sebastian Parrilla Simione, better known as ‘Sebas’.

The little-known Argentinian, a 49-year-old with a UEFA Pro Licence and love of marathon running and Bruce Springsteen, is his closest confidant and has been by his side ever since they oversaw an unbeaten season for Real Madrid’s Under 14s in 2018-19.

Xabi Alonso's most trusted lieutenant is Sebastian 'Sebas' Parrilla, a 49-year-old Bruce Springsteen fan with a tendency to get fired up on the touchline

Alonso had asked for an experienced aide to assist him at Real, and he was handed Parrilla, who was born in Argentina, raised in Spain, and despite not playing professionally had worked for Madrid’s academy since 2002. Parrilla coached all age ranges, from the Under 11s to the B team.

He had Alonso’s ear as their Under 14s won all but one game, and their bond was strong enough that Parrilla ended his 17-year association with Madrid’s academy when he accompanied his manager to Real Sociedad B in 2019. Then he followed him to Bayer Leverkusen in 2022, back to Real Madrid in 2025, and now Chelsea.

There is a little fire to Parrilla. He is already one caution away from a touchline suspension, having been booked against Tottenham Hotspur and Everton. While the analytical Parrilla prefers a low profile, he is Alonso’s alter ego.

The English winter will not only test Parrilla’s preference for wearing shorts whatever the weather, but also Chelsea's ability to arrest their slump with games coming thick and fast – there are seven Premier League fixtures to tackle between now and 2027, starting with Forest on Friday.

One area of focus on the training field this week has been defence. Chelsea have conceded 20 goals in the Premier League, as many as they have scored. Their shakiness at the back has been their downfall of late, and Parrilla was credited with helping organise the Leverkusen back line which went unbeaten in winning the Bundesliga in 2023-24.

When Leverkusen won 5-1 away at Eintracht Frankfurt in May 2024 to maintain their Invincibles tag with two games to go, Alonso was serving a touchline ban. Parrilla manned the technical area and after full time, Granit Xhaka and Co celebrated by pouring water over him.

Parrilla was fine with that, but less pleased during the game with how they conceded a goal from a corner to Hugo Ekitike and gifted other chances to Omar Marmoush.

One source at Leverkusen that we consulted this week credited Parrilla with improving players individually and taking the lead on set-pieces.

When Leverkusen scored from one corner routine against Hoffenheim in November 2023, Parrilla was the architect. He had certain players act as barriers to stop defenders from rushing to block the ball as it was rolled to the edge of the box, where Alex Grimaldo was on hand to power home.

Chelsea have their own set-piece specialist in MacPhee, poached from Aston Villa in the summer, so Parrilla has less control over set-pieces at Cobham.

We do not yet know whether Alonso and Parrilla will decide to change Chelsea’s centre backs for Forest. Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana were bullied by Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey and Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the last two losses.

Former Chelsea man Liam Delap is the next No9 to contend with, and won't be short on motivation.

There is the added complication that Fofana has conducted an unauthorised interview, released this week, in which he laughed off Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit after his penalty miss at Liverpool. Chelsea declined to comment when asked whether that would lead to any internal punishment.

Alonso and Parrilla have been joined at the hip since the former began working with Real Madrid's Under 14s in 2018

Levi Colwill was bullied by Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin in Chelsea's humiliating 4-1 loss last weekend

Alonso’s options are limited. Frustrated as he will have been by his side's 4-1 loss to Leeds, he had no senior replacements for Colwill or Fofana to call on from the bench. The only substitute with 'experience' at centre back was 18-year-old Olutayo Subuloye.

Aaron Anselmino, who represented Argentina in the last international break but has not appeared for Chelsea at all this season, did not make the matchday squad.

Maxence Lacroix is still sidelined, but Alonso told us last week he hopes he will return before 2027. Josh Acheampong and Jorrel Hato could be used centrally rather than as full backs.

As well as assisting Alonso, Parrilla acted as a bridge to the academy at Leverkusen, regularly in contact with Sergi Runge when he was head coach of the Under 17s and Under 19s.

Despite the success of the first team, Parrilla never lost the love for coaching youngsters, agreeing to help the Under 8s with community sessions on occasion. Throwing in Subuloye, who was on Chelsea’s pre-season tour in the summer but has yet to appear competitively, would surely be too big of an ask.

Until better options arrive, it would seem Parrilla is having to try to work his magic in the shadows with Colwill and Fofana. Both players know they need to improve – and fast.

Chelsea have headaches on the horizon, with Alejandro Garnacho not their only loan star struggling to convince his new club of his worth.

Garnacho suffered the ultimate indignity when Aston Villa lost 1-0 to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday. Despite Unai Emery being able to name 12 substitutes in Istanbul, he took only 11 with him including two goalkeepers, and still excluded Garnacho. When asked why, Emery said: ‘The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us.’

Garnacho, 22, joined Villa on a season-long loan with a £42.5million conditional obligation dependent upon making a certain number of appearances. It is still not being disclosed how many matches it would take to trigger the clause, which has been described by sources as confidential. Chelsea insiders previously claimed it was easily achievable.

Alejandro Garnacho (right) is one of several Chelsea players having a miserable time out on loan

But Garnacho has appeared only four times in the Premier League this season, and the last of those appearances was a three-minute cameo against Fulham on October 31. He has not yet started a game in any competition.

While there is no break clause in the contract, it is understood it is possible for both Villa and Chelsea to agree to terminate his loan in January. That situation is one to watch.

But Garnacho is not the only problem loanee that Chelsea might need to address in the near future.

Robert Sanchez is on a 'dry' loan at Como, meaning there is no option or obligation to buy. The 29-year-old Spaniard has started just five of 17 games in all competitions this season.

Another goalkeeper, 24-year-old Filip Jorgensen, is on loan at Chelsea’s sister side Strasbourg, who are hovering around the Ligue 1 relegation zone and have hired Vitor Matos out of Swansea to try to lift them. His is also a dry loan.

Mykhailo Mudryk is with Tottenham, where he has only played 16 minutes in total. He is now working his way back from what Roberto De Zerbi described as a ‘stupid’ ankle injury in training.

Spurs hold a lofty £75m option to buy the 25-year-old Ukrainian, who also did an ill-advised interview last week which was not approved by either Tottenham or Chelsea.

Axel Disasi, 28, is at bottom club Crystal Palace on a straightforward loan. If relegated, Disasi is unlikely to consider staying permanently, having made that clear when West Ham dropped down to the Championship last season.

Mykhailo Mudryk (right) is with Tottenham, where he has only played 16 minutes, thanks in part to an injury his boss Roberto De Zerbi described as 'stupid'

Mamadou Sarr (left) is a rare case - a Chelsea loanee who is playing regularly for his new club, Real Sociedad

Benoit Badiashile, 25, is with Napoli, who have a £23.1m option to sign him permanently if they wish but have had a disappointing start in Serie A, lying down in eighth, 14 points behind league leaders Lazio. Badiashile has started three times in the league, and is currently injured.

Mamadou Sarr is with Real Sociedad, a loan which is also believed not to contain an option to buy, but the 21-year-old has been starting regularly for them in La Liga and the Europa League.

Other loans include Dastan Satpayev, the 18-year-old Kazakh who has been given a harsh welcome to English football with Championship strugglers Burnley (and is also injured), and Caleb Wiley, 21, also in the relegation zone with Preston.

#1250. Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick

Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

That is how far United have, once again, fallen. Fans in the Stretford End unfurled their “Standards” banner, bearing the faces of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson.

It was first revealed in December 2021 in Carrick’s final match as interim following Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s sacking. This should be his final game again, under different, more traumatic, circumstances.

If it is, he is going out having made a stand. He dropped Bruno Fernandes for his outspoken comments, aimed directly at Carrick and his tactics, following the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat away to Como on Wednesday.

At 2-0 down here it was telling that Carrick turned to Matheus Cunha when he substituted Youri Tielemans, who had been so terribly slow and ineffective, at half-time. Carrick did not bring on Fernandes. And he did not turn to the captain after, as he made four substitutions, including bringing on 19-year-old Shea Lacey. That said it all.

The television cameras catching Omar Berrada, the United chief executive, shaking his head in the stands as Carrick’s team gave away goals also told its own story. They have two wins from 12 in all competitions and none in eight. They have only beaten newly promoted Ipswich Town, in August, and Azerbaijan minnows Sabah this season. United were so careless it looked like they could not care less.

There was no guarantee, after Como, that Carrick would remain in charge after this game. So, losing and losing so embarrassingly – it was three, it should have been five – has to have obvious consequences. However cherished Carrick is. However much the fans excuse him. Yes, he has not been helped enough, but he has also not been good enough.

Finishing third and qualifying for the Champions League last season has proved to be the kind of bounce a new manager can achieve, after the pressure was relieved by the sacking of Ruben Amorim, rather than something more sustainable. There was always the fear that Carrick, despite his playing pedigree, might be out of his depth in this job. And so it is proving to be. Especially as he has been hung out to dry. Carrick certainly appeared resigned to his fate.

But what is he coaching? What is he trying to do with United? How does he want his team to play? Yes, there are limitations, but they are badly set up, tactically poor, and struggle to build attacks. The players are not responding, but it does not mean Carrick is blameless.

Bournemouth were not just collectively and individually better – and despite how good they are, that is some indictment of United – but better organised. They knew what they were doing, believed in it and relished it as they collected a fourth victory, and a fourth clean sheet in a row, after a slow start under Marco Rose, the new head coach. It was no shock.

The nature of the goals spoke volumes. For the first, a free-kick was needlessly conceded by Ayden Heaven, who endured a particularly difficult game, as he lunged in recklessly, forcing Evanilson to jump out of the way or risk injury.

Justin Kluivert whipped the ball in beyond the far post and it was met by Rayan, who volleyed in low and precise. The Brazilian was unmarked. Carrick protested – at what? – and the Bournemouth supporters sang “you’re getting sacked in the morning”.

What a finish from Rayan to give Bournemouth the lead! 🔥 https://t.co/9BV0G5Tqgi

The outstanding Rayan should have had a hat-trick but failed to take two chances in the second half, when he only had goalkeeper Senne Lammens to beat, after Bournemouth had already doubled their lead. It came as Leny Yoro slipped over and presented the ball straight to Adrien Truffert, who squared it for Marcus Tavernier to side-foot home. It was that ridiculously easy.

The third was the same, with Evanilson chasing down a ball forward by Tyler Adams. The striker should not have got there. But Harry Maguire, captain in Fernandes’s absence, gave up, pointing at Lammens to win it. Instead, the goalkeeper was beaten to the ball and Evanilson’s finish from an angle, arcing high into the net, was superb.

"What a finish!" 😮‍💨 Evanilson makes it 3-0 to Bournemouth with a stunning goal https://t.co/hPMR78Z3cX

“You’re going down with the City,” goaded the Bournemouth fans and it is that end of the table United need to fret about. Which means, for Carrick, it has to be over. The Stretford End sang his name. But it was out of support for him as a player, his reputation, what he represented, not what is happening now as they once again vented their anger at the owners, director of football, Jason Wilcox, and even the plans for a new stadium.

It was the same as Carrick walked down the tunnel, thumping his chest as his name was sung. Then it turned. The vitriol, frustration and anger dripped down on the players, washing them away.

This felt like a new nadir. And the need for yet another new start away to Chelsea on Saturday.

Former Tottenham defender speaking to the BBC:

Manchester United’s players were just standing there today. I did not see in their body language that they are prepared to do everything for the manager, the club or the fans to change their situation.

It’s an easy thing to say they are lacking leaders but it’s true. They just don’t have big characters. It is not something technical but if you are in a tunnel and you saw the likes of [former Man Utd defenders] Nemanja Vidic or Rio Ferdinand their body language told the opposition that they were going to have a tough afternoon.

Carrick admits he does not know if he will remain in place.

The club have a week off now, with the next match a trip to Stamford Bridge against a tasty Chelsea side, albeit one who lost to Spurs last night.

He says: “It’s a tough situation. What is next? I don’t know. I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility. But we’ll have to wait and see.”

Carrick gives a non-answer over his choice to leave Fernandes on the bench.

He says: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference but those are the decisions we made today.”

Carrick then denies that his acknowledgement of the crowd was to say goodbye, adding: “It wasn’t a farewell from me. I’m mixed emotions, I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell.

“Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.”

Carrick also tells Sky: “It’s really difficult to have a day like this at this football club and feel the emotion and dynamics of what it was like today.

“Not for me personally but for Manchester United. It was really mixed. I feel responsibility with the position I’m in. I’ve been at the club a long time. It hurts a lot going through this.”

Carrick potentially acknowledges that his time is up, telling Sky: “It was a strange, mixed of emotions at the end of the game. It wasn’t a nice way to end the game.

“It was a tough day for the players. We went into the game having been rocked. You can feel that. They’re really hurting and disappointed in there. It’s not a nice feeling. You have to accept it, we’re in that situation.”

Today’s United captain Harry Maguire tells Sky Sports: “It wasn’t good enough. Disappointed to give a goal away so early - another set play - and conceding first in the Premier League it makes it difficult.

“A mistake for the second makes it hard for ourselves. We didn’t perform well enough as individuals or as a team and we didn’t deserve anything from the game.

“It’s not clicking at the moment. Results are not good enough and performances in the last week not good enough. Still early in the season.

“Got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror - that’s the most important thing - think what you can do more and what more you can contribute to the team and if we do that we’ll get somewhere.”

United players have said this for some time now. Each season they look in the mirror, and each season the supporters get the same.

Telegraph columnist Jamie Carragher thinks Carrick has had enough after that.

His emotional exit after the match suggested as much, with the former Liverpool player telling Sky: “He wants to be put out of his misery tonight.”

The fact that a mid-table team can come to Old Trafford and leave with three points is no longer a surprise.

If anything, it’s unusual when competent teams struggle against United these days.

Quite how replacing a manager changes a decade of falling short solves things, who knows?

At least the scoreline is not a surprise. Bournemouth always tend to win 3-0 at Old Trafford these days

Arne Slot underwhelmed last season, and Liverpool moved swiftly to appoint Andoni Iraola from Bournemouth.

They have defeated an impressive Brighton side 2-0 today, and you can read our report here.

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young is scathing about the players who have succeeded him.

“But the players on the pitch showed nothing. They didn’t run, they didn’t look like a team together.

Bruno Fernandes has been dropped for Manchester United’s crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Michael Carrick has taken the decision to drop the United captain to the bench in the wake of his public criticism on Wednesday following the shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics and has now been taken out of the starting XI.

The move had looked likely with Carrick refusing to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy when quizzed on the matter on Friday.

Carrick had responded to Fernandes questioning the set up and approach by suggesting tactics can go out of the window when players are unprepared to run.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

With just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

In stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

#1249. Toni Kroos Believes Arsenal Only Have 2 ‘World Class’ Players

Toni Kroos has revealed his belief that Arsenal only have two 'world-class' players in their midst, and Declan Rice isn't one of them.

Mikel Arteta's men won the Premier League title last season and were only denied a historic double by a penalty shootout, losing on spot-kicks to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final in Budapest in May. The Gunners are on course to retain their crown as champions of England, as they currently sit six points clear, while many have tipped them to go all the way in Europe's elite club competition this term.

The North Londoners boast an embarrassment of riches across the pitch, with this deep and talented squad ultimately leading to all this success.

Despite this, six-time Champions League winner Kroos doesn't think there are more than two world-class players in Arteta's squad.

World-class has made its way into football's lexicon and is now considered an exclusive bracket of players that only the very elite on the planet fit into. However, a universal definition has never been established, despite many people arguing effusively whenever someone makes a claim about a player being world-class or not being world-class.

Ultimately, it can be assumed that the best teams in Europe all contain a multitude of world-class players, although Kroos doesn't believe so.

Speaking in an interview with Luppen TV, the former Real Madrid midfielder named David Raya and William Saliba as Arsenal's sole 'world-class' players, snubbing Rice in the process.

The former Liverpool defender has caused confusion amongst the Arsenal fanbase following his comments about the side.

"I’m also in agreement that Arsenal are a world-class team for me, but not one studded with tons of world-class players,” he said.

Kroos added that he agreed with compatriots Mats Hummels and Kramer's take on Prime that Saliba is 'absolutely world-class', before disagreeing with the pair, who claimed that the Frenchman is the only Gunners player who falls into this category: “So, I’m not quite there, because I think, for example, Raya is also a world-class goalkeeper."

Asked about Rice and Martin Odegaard, the German said the pair are 'a bit behind that, but not as absolute world-class'.

"I believe that it is a world-class team in how they play together and how they function together. They’ve shown that.”

Just last month, Rice was nominated for the Ballon d'Or, with the only other midfielders who were up for the award being Rodri, Fabian Ruiz, Jude Bellingham, Vitinha, Joao Neves and Bruno Fernandes.

Clearly, the general perception is that Rice is among the best few players in his position in the world, which would qualify him for a 'world-class' tag in many people's eyes.

Equally, Gabriel Magalhaes was also nominated for the Ballon d'Or, and was also snubbed by Kroos, while Bukayo Saka wasn't mentioned at all by the legendary deep-lying playmaker.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1248. Augmenting reality with integrated photonics

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 915–926 (2026) Cite this article

Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

#1247. Hull City drop Roma loanee Robinio Vaz after Paris police incident

Roma loanee Robinio Vaz has been left out of Hull City’s squad for Sunday’s Premier League game against Crystal Palace after an incident in Paris this week.

According to talkSPORT, the 19-year-old forward was reportedly detained by French police on suspicion of fraud involving a hire car. The car had been flagged as stolen because its owner had missed lease payments. Vaz was released without charge after the matter was dropped. However, Hull say they did not know he had travelled to France.

Hull coach Sergej Jakirović told the BBC he only found out when Robinio Vaz failed to turn up for training on Tuesday.

“It’s not good behaviour, I can say like this. It’s not professional,” he said. “I know he is young, but you are a professional player, you need to be very, very careful especially in private life.”

Jakirović confirmed Hull are now in talks with Roma to find a solution. “He is not our player, he is on loan here, so it’s a Roma decision,” he added.

Roma signed Vaz from Marseille in January for a fee reported at around €25m. He then joined Hull on a season-long loan with an option to buy on deadline day. Things have not gone to plan in England, though. He has made only five substitute appearances, totalling around 50 minutes, and has been unable to dislodge Oli McBurnie.

#1246. What's wrong with Erling Haaland? Man City's superstar has been radiating an air of gloom in front of the cameras - but it's his form on the pitch that should most concern Enzo Maresca, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 08:22 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:10 EST, 25 November 2026

A smile did eventually spread across the face of Erling Haaland when dissecting Manchester City’s draw with Napoli, stretching their worrying run to one victory in five games.

Not for the first time in recent weeks, he had appeared morose and despondent, radiating an air of gloom, talking about how the team are ‘questioning anything’ amid these results. That’s not exactly inspiring confidence among their supporters.

But just as City’s captain for the night was about to finish his media duties before heading home, one final question focused on Sunday’s clash with Arsenal and a rivalry with a ‘certain centre half’. Haaland’s mood changed instantly.

‘It's always good to play against the best teams,’ said the Norwegian, breaking out into a smirk as he allowed the impending battle with Gabriel to percolate.

‘Arsenal were the best team last year and one of the best in the last five years now, so it's fun to play against them and it’s always fun to play against Gabriel.’

There was, at last, some positive emotion. Is Gabriel and that playground scrapping what he needs to re-energise? We’ll find out in a few days.

Erling Haaland appeared morose and despondent following Man City's draw with Napoli, suggesting he was 'questioning everything' amid their worrying run of form

Haaland did raise a smile about the prospect of his impending battle with Arsenal defender Gabriel this weekend

The Man City star has shown increasing dejected body language during games and has spent too much time recently with his head bowed and hand waving at team-mates

Haaland talked about City needing to be at their maximum to take anything from the Emirates this weekend. Whether that is ‘fun’ or not is a different matter entirely, but what Enzo Maresca must demand more from all of his players. Even with 14 goals already this term, that includes Haaland.

He is leading from the front off the pitch. Standing in front of the cameras more than anyone else, facing up to the dipping form and taking on those responsibilities without complaining. The forward wrote on X on Wednesday afternoon: 'Together through the ups and downs. Thank you for pushing us until the very end yesterday. Full focus on Sunday now.'

Yet City need more of that leadership between the white lines from somebody who has drawn a blank in four of his last five club matches, despite scoring three times over the international break.

There is too much head bowing and hand waving at the moment.

The 26-year-old admits he has to give extra. And believes that the team are generally creating enough chances for him, even if the freewheeling attacking abandon of early season has vanished.

City's results are clearly affecting Haaland’s mood and that can be self-perpetuating. He admits that failing to reverse this run is hurting him. That is evident by watching his increasingly dejected body language during games and the frustration seen when he gestured at Abdukodir Khusanov as the defender dithered with a routine throw-in during Saturday’s draw against Fulham. It wasn’t the picture of a man happy with his lot.

Only Haaland will know whether that general angst is contributing to a lack of intensity in his own performances. Nobody has mentioned the striker carrying a knock, although Maresca has appeared focused on offering him rest whenever possible over the past three months.

Something is undoubtedly proving an obstacle for him. He’s insisted that it isn’t the guilty verdicts hanging over City and, listening to him, the gripes and disappointment look focused on City’s lack of control in games. It also cannot help that Haaland will feel aggrieved to have seen a goal on Saturday chalked off for a foul on Bernd Leno and then to have not been awarded a penalty for grappling on Tuesday night.

If both or even one of those decisions go his way, the interview that sparked concern with fans – one conducted almost immediately after full time when emotions are at their highest – would likely have been very different.

City will have to cling on to the idea that a sullen Haaland is at least a Haaland who cares. And a Haaland who cares must surely dig them out of this hole, even if he cannot do that alone.

#1245. He was Team-Mates With Virgil van Dijk - Police Found him with £3.1k-worth of Cocaine

The climb to the very top of the Premier League is full of landmarks and sightseeing opportunities. Once that mountain peak arrives, however, the only way is down and the sightseeing opportunities quickly turn into dangerous cliff edges. The glory is so often torn down quicker than it had originally been built up.

The likes of Raheem Sterling and Dele Alli have fallen by the wayside in recent years. Sterling went from glory at Manchester City to struggles at Arsenal and Chelsea, before pleading guilty to dangerous driving and nitrous oxide offences in 2026 and receiving a 12-month suspended sentence.

Alli was tipped to be the next best thing by many. In 2026, he is a free agent and has turned to Twitch streaming.

Both are devastating cases with their own story, which have followed a similar path to Anthony Stokes' dramatic fall from grace.

Stokes had the world at his feet at just 14 years old when he completed a move to Arsenal from Shelbourne in 2003. He very much looked destined to become the next big Irish talent, especially after a loan spell with Scottish side Falkirk ended with 14 goals in 16 appearances three years later.

What followed should have been his rise to the top. Instead, the striker's career began to suffer a dramatic fall off - starting with a difficult move to Sunderland.

After arriving for £2m, Stokes failed to live up to expectations and scored just three goals in 36 appearances. Loan moves to Crystal Palace and Sheffield United then failed to revive his career in English football and a return to Scotland followed.

It was there that Stokes found his feet again, scoring 22 goals in 44 games for Hibernian and then racking up 135 appearances for Celtic and scoring a further 58 goals. Alas, that would be as good as it would get for the forward, who went onto score a total of just 25 goals for his next nine clubs.

Stokes' failed potential will hurt him more than anyone else, especially after Celtic where he was teammates with Virgil van Dijk and finally at his best.

What followed a disappointing career was even more devastating than the career itself. In 2024, Stokes pleaded guilty to unlawful possession of cocaine at the value of £3.1k, which had been hidden in a sock, and having the drug for sale or supply.

The former Arsenal prospect also admitted driving while over the alcohol limit and four counts of dangerous driving, as well as not producing a driving licence and not having motor insurance.

Stokes originally received a 15-month sentence with a five-year road ban, before an appeal spared him prison time altogether. Judge Jonathan Dunphy instead ordered a suspended sentence and 240 hours of community service, claiming that the former Premier League forward had "a lot to offer once he sorts out his difficulties.”

The court heard that Stokes' drinking problem started during his playing days after "too much too soon" as a young prospect, who uprooted his life to join Arsenal at just 14.

After the incident, Stokes signed for a pub team for Conor McGregor’s Black Forge Inn boozer, returning to football outside a professional level for the first time since 2020.

A former Arsenal player, who played alongside Jack Wilshere and Cesc Fabregas, was sentenced to four years in prison back in 2025.

#1244. Ronaldo reveals why he left Barcelona for Inter in 1997

Ronaldo has revealed that money was the main reason he left Barcelona for Inter in 1997, with the Nerazzurri offering him four times his salary at the Camp Nou.

The Brazilian legend was speaking on the Stick to Football podcast with Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher, in a special episode released today on Disney+.

Ronaldo spent just one season at Barcelona after joining from PSV, but it was a spectacular one. He scored goal after goal in La Liga and the Cup Winners’ Cup before Inter paid his release clause to bring him to Serie A.

“Barça bought me for 20 million, and I received a good chunk of that. There, I was earning two million a year, and Inter offered me eight, so I decided to go,” he explained.

Ronaldo said he was still angry about the 1996 Ballon d’Or, when he was voted in second place behind Matthias Sammer.

“I lost it to Sammer, who was a defender. I was angry because I’d played fantastically with Barcelona and scored so many goals,” he said.

He made up for it in his first season in Milan, winning the Ballon d’Or in 1997 as an Inter player. He won it again in 2002.

Il Fenomeno also suggested modern forwards don’t know how lucky they are.

“Today’s strikers have an easier life than we did. I’d have liked to have the same protection. We suffered so much. Our generation was full of killers, and nobody protected us,” he said with a laugh.

Ronaldo was less upbeat about the Brazil national team. He admitted Argentina’s fighting spirit is “painful” to watch for Brazilians.

“I think we’re copying European players. Before, there was always very high confidence in our country based purely on our talent. But Europeans today are stronger, faster, more organised, and play better,” he said. “Brazil aren’t strong enough to win the World Cup. We don’t have a strong team, we’re not united.”
